summary: Five independent reviewers attack the DEMIURGE specs from different angles before the parallel build

issues.where: SPEC-SIM §2 (`phase` row), §3.3 (`vars.seaBase`, `vars.iceRef`), §3.10 (`awaken`, `comet`), §3.12 (Sim API, Phases, Tick order); FOUNDATION §5.2 (`world.vars`, `seaLevel`)
issues.problem: The genesis-to-history hand-off has no owner. (a) `awaken` is in powers.js and "the first use starts 'history'", but Sim exposes no phase setter (`genesis.next` only covers water->life and life->people) and `phase` is listed as emitted by sim. Powers will write `world.phase` directly, so no `phase` event fires: game.js `armForPhase`, the HUD genesis card and Audio never hear it. (b) `vars.seaBase` and `vars.iceRef` are read by `Climate.yearly` (and by the HUD's sea-level change) but no module is told to write them. tests/helpers/world.js sets `seaBase` by hand, which hides this in unit tests. In the real game the first yearly computes `undefined + ...` = NaN, `seaLevel` becomes NaN, every `elev < seaLevel` is false and the oceans vanish; `iceRef` 0 or undefined gives 0/0. (c) The tick order is given for 'history' only. "The environment runs in every phase after molten" does not say whether `Climate.yearly`, `Powers.natural`, `Civ/Society.yearly` or snapshots run in genesis. If `Climate.yearly` runs in 'water' it fights the comet for `seaLevel` (two writers); if `Powers.natural` runs, the tutorial gets random eruptions. (d) `Sim.create` does not say it calls `Sim.use`, and game.js calls only `Sim.create` for new worlds, so Chronicle is never attached for them.
issues.fix: Add to §3.12: `Sim.setPhase(world, phase) -> bool` - the ONLY writer of `world.phase`; runs entry actions, then emits `phase {phase, prev}`. Entry actions: 'water': heat = 0. 'life': vars.lifeBoost = TUNE.sim.lifeBoost (about 25). 'people': vars.lifeBoost = 1. 'history': vars.lifeBoost = 1; `Climate.baseline(world)`; year = 0. `genesis.next`, `genesis.skip` and the `awaken` power (after its first successful `Civ.found` while phase === 'people') all go through it. Add to §3.3: `Climate.baseline(world)` - sets ice to its equilibrium in one step, then `vars.seaBase = seaLevel` and `vars.iceRef = max(1e-3, land-ice volume)`. `Climate.yearly` leaves `seaLevel` alone while `vars.seaBase` is undefined. Add to §3.5: `Life.fill(world, frac = 1)` - set veg = frac x capacity and fauna to capacity on all plantable land (used by `genesis.skip`; budget for `Sim.create` + `skip` is 600 ms at L 6 because the title screen runs it at boot). Per-phase tick table: molten = heat only. water/life/people = Powers.tick, Life.burn, Life.step, Climate.stepIce and the flag-driven derive/climate/hydro/classify/habitability passes; NOT Units.step, Civ.yearly, Society.yearly, Climate.yearly, Powers.natural, snapshots or checkEnding. history/ended = full order. `seaLevel` writers: Powers (comet) and `genesis.skip` before history, `Climate.yearly` only in history/ended. "`Sim.create` ends by calling `Sim.use(world)`." Also compute the lapse rate from height above `max(seaLevel, -3.5)`; with the -9 start every land cell is about 50 C colder and the planet ices over before the first comet.

issues.where: FOUNDATION §5.2 (`world.rivers`) vs SPEC-SIM §3.4 (Hydro) vs SPEC-RENDER §6 (rivers) and §11 (Fixtures)
issues.problem: Three shapes for one field. FOUNDATION: "array of Int32Array cell polylines, source -> mouth". SPEC-SIM §3.4: array of `{ cells: Int32Array, flow: Float32Array }`. SPEC-RENDER: ribbons "width from flow" along `world.rivers`. Hydro, Planet and Fixtures authors each read a different document. Either `rivers[i].cells` is undefined and Planet.sync throws, or `rivers[i].length` is undefined and no river is ever drawn. A throw inside `Renderer.frame` is caught by game.js's per-frame try/catch every frame, so nothing renders at all.
issues.fix: FOUNDATION §5.2 line becomes: `world.rivers = []   derived: array of { cells: Int32Array, flow: Float32Array } (equal length, source -> mouth, flow = discharge at each cell); see SPEC-SIM §3.4`. Add to SPEC-RENDER §6 and the Fixtures paragraph: "River shape is the one in SPEC-SIM §3.4. Fixtures must produce exactly that shape. Planet treats a missing or empty list as no rivers and never throws on it."

issues.where: SPEC-SIM §2 (`ending`, `ark:launched`, `nuke` rows), §3.12 (Endings, `Sim.checkEnding`); FOUNDATION §5.2 (`world.ending`); SPEC-UI §5 (`Screens.ending`), §7 (ending stingers)
issues.problem: The ending has no agreed shape or data path. §2 says the `ending` payload is `{ type, culture }`; §3.12 says `{ type: 'ark', mood }` and `{ type: 'silence' }` with `mood: 'ash'` only in one case (otherwise undefined). `Screens.ending(ending)` picks text "by type/mood" and Audio plays "ending (one per mood)", but an Audio handler on the `ending` event gets no mood, and Screens gets no culture. `Sim.checkEnding` is polled yearly, yet Ark completion is signalled only by the Bus event `ark:launched` from Society, and "a nuclear exchange in the last 200 years" is recorded nowhere. Nothing stops `ark:launched` re-firing every year once `ark >= 1`, or a second ending during Keep playing.
issues.fix: Paste into §3.12 and FOUNDATION §5.2: `world.ending = { type: 'ark' | 'silence', mood: 'beloved' | 'feared' | 'forgotten' | 'parting' | 'quiet' | 'ash', culture: id | -1, settlement: id | -1, year }`. The `ending` event payload is exactly this object (replace `{ type, culture }` in §2). Society writes `world.vars.ark = { culture, settlement, year }` when it emits `ark:launched`, and does so only once per world (while `vars.ark` is undefined). Society writes `world.vars.lastNuke = world.year` with every `nuke`. `Sim.checkEnding` reads those two vars (no Bus subscription) and returns null when `world.ending` is already set. 'quiet' = silence with no nuke in the last 200 years. Mean devotion and love are population-weighted over the launching culture's live settlements.

issues.where: SPEC-SIM §3.12 (Tick order, `Sim.rederive`), §0.8 (budget), §3.2 (`Terrain.touched`); FOUNDATION §5.2 (`world.need`)
issues.problem: The tick order breaks a dependency and stacks every heavy pass on one tick. (a) `Hydro.update` runs after `Life.classify` and `Life.habitability`, and nothing re-runs them afterwards. Biomes and `hab` are therefore computed from the previous `fresh` and `water`. After `Sim.create` or a load those are the defaults (`fresh` = 255, `water` = 0): WETLAND and "fresh water within 2 hops makes a desert liveable" fail, and `Civ.bestSite` inside `genesis.skip` picks the first tribe's home from that `hab`. `Sim.rederive`'s order is not given at all. (b) At tick % 40 === 0 the schedule runs the yearly group, `stepIce`, `Climate.update` (up to 12 ms), classify, habitability and possibly `Hydro.update` (up to 15 ms) together, against "any single tick <= 30 ms" and "must not all land on the same tick"; game.js budgets 6 ms of sim per frame. (c) `Terrain.touched` sets all three need flags on every frame the sculpt brush is held, and unlike hydro, `Climate.update` has no minimum interval, so it runs every tick while sculpting.
issues.fix: FOUNDATION: `world.need = { derive, climate, hydro, life }`. `Climate.update` and `Hydro.update` set `need.life` when they finish; `Life.habitability` clears it. `Sim.rederive` order (binding): Terrain.derive -> Climate.update -> Hydro.update -> Life.classify -> Life.habitability -> Life.rebuild -> Civ.rebuild. Replace the tail of the tick order with: "... -> when tick % 4 === 0: the yearly group -> when tick % 20 === 10: Climate.stepIce -> then, on ticks where tick % 4 !== 0, at most ONE heavy pass, the first that is due: (1) need.derive: Terrain.derive; (2) need.climate and at least 8 ticks since the last Climate.update, or 40 ticks since the last one: Climate.update; (3) need.hydro and at least 8 ticks since the last: Hydro.update; (4) need.life: Life.classify on this tick and Life.habitability on the next."

issues.where: SPEC-SIM §1 (`Settlement.capital`, `Culture.capital`, `Culture.pop/towns/dead`), §2 (`culture:died` row "society / civ"), §3.7 (Civ.found, launch "capital only"), §3.8 (New cultures, The Ark)
issues.problem: Nobody owns capitals or culture membership. `Settlement.capital` and `Culture.capital` duplicate each other and no function is told to set either: `Civ.found` does not mention it, and nothing re-elects after `Civ.destroy`, `Civ.capture` or a schism. `b.launch` is "capital only" and the Ark needs the capital, so once a culture's first capital is drowned, cratered or captured, that culture can never reach the 'ark' ending. For a schism Society must move settlements to the daughter culture, but the only API is `Civ.capture`, which emits `settlement:captured` (Chronicle will narrate a conquest). `culture:died` is listed as "society / civ": both will emit it or neither will. `Culture.pop` and `towns` are "refreshed yearly" by an unnamed module, and Society's war logic and the HUD read them.
issues.fix: Add to §3.7: `Civ.setCulture(world, s, cultureId)` - change membership without conquest (schisms); no `settlement:captured`; sets dirty.objects and dirty.color. `Civ.electCapital(world, cultureId) -> settlement id | -1` - the most populous live settlement; writes `culture.capital` and `s.capital` for every settlement of that culture. Rules: "Civ is the only writer of `s.culture`, `s.capital`, `culture.capital`, `culture.pop`, `culture.towns`, `culture.dead`. `Civ.found` makes a culture's first settlement its capital. `Civ.destroy`, `Civ.capture` and `Civ.setCulture` call `electCapital` for every culture they affect. `b.launch` and `ark` do not move with the capital: a new capital builds its own launch site and `ark` restarts at 0. At the end of `Civ.yearly`: refresh `culture.pop` and `culture.towns`; a culture with no live settlement and no settler unit of its own gets `dead = true` and Civ emits `culture:died`, exactly once." In §2 split the row: `culture:died`, `culture:age`, `world:age` are all emitted by civ.

issues.where: SPEC-SIM §1 (Settlement `plague`, `immune`, `blessed`, `inspire`, `b`), §2 (`settlement:plague`, `settlement:building`), §3.7 (Growth, Buildings), §3.8 (Trade, Ark), §3.10 (plague, heal, natural outbreaks); FOUNDATION §5.2 (`world.stats`, `world.god`)
issues.problem: Settlement status fields have several writers and no owner. `plague` is written by Powers (`plague = 0.6`, heal, natural outbreaks), by Society (trader arrival: "plague may hop") and by Civ (neighbour spread, fading; Civ's text also claims spread "along trade"). `settlement:plague {id, start}` is emitted "by civ" only, so miracle plagues and cures produce no event (no chronicle line, no miasma, no toll), and direct writers bypass `immune`. The countdowns `blessed`, `inspire`, `immune` ("years remaining") have no decrementer: Civ reads them, Powers sets them, and either both yearly passes decrement or neither does (permanent blessing). `b.launch` is claimed by both §3.7 and §3.8. `b.wonder` is set by Society with no `settlement:building`. `stats.wars`, `stats.miracles`, `stats.believers`, `god.mercy`, `god.wrath` and `god.epithet` have no named writer, yet the HUD shows the epithet.
issues.fix: Add to §3.7: `Civ.infect(world, s, severity = 0.6) -> bool` - false if dead or `immune > 0`; `plague = max(plague, severity)`; emits `settlement:plague {id, start: true}` when plague was 0. `Civ.cure(world, s, immuneYears = 30) -> bool` - `plague = 0`, `immune = immuneYears`; emits `{id, start: false}` if it was above 0. "Powers (plague, heal, natural outbreaks) and Society (traders) must call these and never write `plague` or `immune`." Ownership table: Civ.yearly owns pop, K, growth, tier, radius, famine, plague fading (calls `cure` below 0.05) and spread to settlements within 8 hops; decrements `blessed`, `inspire`, `immune` by 1 per year (floor 0); owns every `b.*` except wonder and emits `settlement:building` for each, launch included. Society owns devotion, love, `b.wonder` (emits both `wonder:built` and `settlement:building {building: 'wonder'}`), `ark` (advances only while `b.launch === 1`), prophet, edict, exhaustion, relations, `road`; `stats.wars++` in `declareWar`. Powers.use does `stats.miracles++` and `god.deeds[id]++` once per `power:used` emission and may set `blessed` and `inspire`. Sim.refreshStats owns `stats.pop`, `peakPop`, `believers` (sum of pop x devotion). `Chronicle.updateEpithets` writes `culture.epithet` and `god.epithet` (the epithet of the most populous living culture). `Society.witness` adds `max(0, good) x faith` to `god.mercy` and `max(0, -good) x faith` to `god.wrath`.

issues.where: SPEC-SIM §3.8 (`Society.witness`), §3.10 (`Powers.use`, brush powers), §2 (`awe:short`, `power:used`); SPEC-UI §4 (Toasts), §7 (deny sound)
issues.problem: The witness contract has no units, and brush powers call it per frame. `Society.witness(world, cell, ang, { kind, awe, good })` does `devotion += awe x falloff`. That `awe` is a devotion delta on a 0..1 scale, but it carries the name of the Awe currency, whose costs run 5 to 250. A Powers author passing the cost (150 for a meteor) sets every witness's devotion to 1 on every use. `kind` is undefined. Brush powers call `Powers.use` every frame, so as written `witness` runs every frame (devotion gain scales with frame rate, 60 vs 144 fps), `god.deeds[id]` counts frames rather than "times used" (epithets read it), and `awe:short` fires every frame while the button is held with an empty meter: 60 "Not enough Awe" toasts and deny sounds per second.
issues.fix: Rename and define: `Society.witness(world, cell, ang, { kind, faith, good })` - `kind` = power id (or 'nuke'); `faith` = devotion gained at the centre, 0..0.3, already multiplied by elapsed seconds for brush powers; `good` in -1..1. Starting table (TUNE.powers.faith): rain 0.02/s, bloom 0.02/s, raise and lower 0.01/s, lightning 0.03, quake 0.06, plague 0.04, meteor 0.12, volcano 0.15, heal 0.08, inspire 0.06, prophet 0.10, peace 0.06. Add to §3.10: "For brush powers, Powers accumulates dt and, on the same cadence as `power:used` (at most 4 per real second), calls `Society.witness` once with the accumulated faith and counts one deed. `awe:short` is emitted at most once per 1.5 real seconds per power id, timed with a clock advanced in `Powers.update`."

issues.where: FOUNDATION §5.2 (Transient caches); SPEC-SIM §1 (`_cells`, `_n`), §3.5 (`world._fires`), §3.7 (`Civ.claim`), §3.11 (`culture._seen`), §3.12 (`Sim.rederive`); SPEC-RENDER §10 (fires); SPEC-UI §7 (fire ambience)
issues.problem: Transient caches have no rebuild contract. (a) Chronicle is told to track what each culture witnessed in `culture._seen` "or world.vars". Underscore fields are never serialized and must be rebuildable from persisted state; this one is not, so epithets reset on every Continue. No module is assigned to write it either: Chronicle only hears `power:used {id, cell, ang, brush}` and would have to redo Powers' decision of who witnessed. (b) `Sim.rederive` must rebuild "every transient cache" but the owners expose nothing to call. `world._fires` (Life) has no stated format, yet FX ("flames and smoke on burning cells") and Audio ("crackle near fires") need the burning cells and may not scan the planet per frame. `settlement._cells/_n` can only be rebuilt through `Civ.claim`, which re-decides ownership ("not owned by another settlement" is order-dependent) and rewrites the persisted `owner[]`, so a loaded world diverges from the one that was saved. (c) Module-level scratch (Path heap and stamps, Hydro buffers) will be sized once, but the title world is L 6 and tests use L 4.
issues.fix: Add `seen: {}` to Culture in §1 (persisted; kind -> accumulated faith witnessed) and to §3.8: "`Society.witness` adds `faith x falloff` to `culture.seen[kind]` for the culture of each witnessing settlement." In §3.11 replace "tracked in `culture._seen` or `world.vars`" with "read from `culture.seen` and `god.deeds`". Add to §3.5: "`world._fires = { cells: Int32Array, n }` (binding; `cells[0..n-1]` have `fire > 0`). `Life.rebuild(world)` rebuilds it from `fire[]`." Add to §3.7: "`Civ.rebuild(world)` rebuilds `_cells/_n` of every live settlement from `owner[]` without changing `owner`." `Sim.rederive` calls both after the derived passes. Add to §0: "Consumers treat a missing `_fires` or `_cells` as empty. Module-level scratch buffers are keyed by `world.n` and re-allocated when it changes."

issues.where: SPEC-SIM §3.10 (`Powers.update`, `Powers.use`), §3.12 (Sim.tick, Headless tools), §4 (cruel policy); SPEC-UI §0 (`debug.ff`, `debug.use`)
issues.problem: Comets and meteors never land outside the frame loop. `Powers.update(world, realDt)` advances their flight and is called only by Game's requestAnimationFrame loop; `Sim.tick` does not call it. `tools/simrun.js` policies call `Powers.use('meteor')` and the impact never happens, so the `cruel` balance target cannot be measured. `DM.debug.ff(years)` in game.js runs only `Sim.tick`, so the documented test recipe (`debug.use('meteor', cell)` then `debug.ff`) fast-forwards with the meteor frozen in the sky. Impact tick also depends on frame timing, which breaks "same inputs at the same ticks give an identical world".
issues.fix: Add to §3.10: "`Powers.use(world, id, cell, { ang, dt, instant = false })` - with `instant`, comet and meteor impact immediately (no flight, no `meteor:launched`)." Add to §3.12: "`Sim.tick` never calls `Powers.update`. Any caller that ticks without the frame loop (tools/simrun.js, tools/policies.js, `DM.debug.ff`, `Sim.genesis.skip`, tests) calls `Powers.update(world, 0.125)` after every `Sim.tick` (one tick is 0.125 real seconds at 1x), or uses `instant: true`." The lead updates `D.ff` in game.js to match.

issues.where: FOUNDATION §5.2 (`world.dirty`); SPEC-SIM §0.7, §3.2 (`Terrain.touched`), §3.5 (dirty.objects); SPEC-RENDER §4 step 1, §6 (`Planet.sync`), §9 (`Objects.sync`)
issues.problem: Dirty flags are cleared by the first consumer, and trees do not follow the ground. Objects places trees and buildings on `Planet.groundAt` and rebuilds only on `dirty.objects`. `Terrain.touched` sets `dirty.elev/water/color` but not `objects`. `Planet.sync` runs before `Objects.sync` and clears `dirty.elev` ("clear what you handled"), so Objects can never see an elevation change. After raise, lower, quake, crater or cone, trees and houses stay at their old radius: floating over craters, buried in raised land. Separately, Life must set `dirty.objects` when veg crosses "visibility thresholds" that exist only inside objects.js.
issues.fix: Add to FOUNDATION §5.2: "Each dirty flag has exactly one consumer, which clears it: Planet owns `elev`, `color`, `water`, `rivers`, `roads`; Objects owns `objects`." Change §3.2: "`Terrain.touched` sets dirty.elev/water/color/objects and need.hydro/climate/derive." Add to §3.3: a sea-level move of more than 0.03 also sets `dirty.objects`. Add to FOUNDATION §5.3: `DM.State.VEG_T = [0.22, 0.5, 0.78]` (veg levels at which a cell shows 1, 2, 3 trees). Life sets `dirty.objects` when a cell crosses one of them; Objects uses the same array. Add to SPEC-RENDER §9: "On `dirty.objects`, Objects re-reads `Planet.groundAt` for every static instance."

issues.where: SPEC-RENDER §1 (`GL.frame.set`), §2 (Frame block: `uFx`, `uWorld`, `uPlanet`, `uTime`), §4 step 1, §6 (`Planet.setOverlay`), §7 (`Sky.update`), §10 (`FX.update`), §11 (Renderer)
issues.problem: The Frame block has no write ownership. `GL.frame.set(name, x, y, z, w)` writes whole vec4s. `uFx` mixes a camera-derived value (x: cloud opacity that fades as the camera descends) with values `Sky.update` is told to set (y cloudiness, z ocean fraction), and `Sky.update(dt, world)` is not given the view. Renderer and Sky will both call `frame.set('uFx', ...)` and zero each other's components: clouds either vanish or never fade. `uWorld.w` (overlay mode) is known only to Planet, because game.js calls `Planet.setOverlay` directly, while the Renderer fills `uWorld`. `uWorld.z` (night-light level), `uPlanet.z/w` (shell radii) and `uTime.z` (cloud drift) have no values and no owner. The four step-1 calls also have two argument orders: `Planet.sync(world, dt)` and `Objects.sync(world, dt)` but `Sky.update(dt, world)` and `FX.update(dt, world)`; a swap fails silently with NaN.
issues.fix: Add to §1: `frame.setComp(name, index, value)` (write one component). Add to §2: "Ownership. `Renderer.frame` writes, before `Sky.update`: the four matrices, uCamPos, uSunDir, uSunCol, uTime (z = real seconds x 0.01), uScreen, uPlanet = (DM.R, world.seaLevel, DM.R + 13, DM.R + 20), uBrush, uBrushCol, uFlash, uFlashCol, uWorld = (world.heat, world.dust, night, DM.Planet ? DM.Planet.overlay : 0) with night = [0, 0.15, 0.3, 0.45, 0.75, 1, 1][world.age], uFx = (1 - smoothstep(0.55, 0.9, zoom01), 0.5, 0.7, 0), and all uStorms zeroed. `Sky.update` then overwrites only uFx.y and uFx.z (via `setComp`) and uStorms (via `setStorm`). No other module writes the Frame block. Renderer uploads after step 1." Add to §6: `Planet.overlay` (read-only current mode). Change the signatures to `Sky.update(world, dt)` and `FX.update(world, dt)`.

issues.where: SPEC-SIM §3.10 (power definition `ang`, `Powers.use({ang, dt})`, meteor "~0.05 rad"); SPEC-UI §0 (`Game.usePower`, `Game.brushAng`), §2 (brush ring; "one letter per power"), §4 (hotkey on button)
issues.problem: The power definition is missing two things Input, HUD, Game and Powers must agree on. Radius: the definition has `ang (default radius)` and `Powers.use` accepts `{ ang }`. game.js passes `ang: G.brushAng` (0.025 to 0.14) for every power, and Input sizes the ring by `Game.brushAng` for every non-settlement power. The Powers author cannot tell whether a click power honours it. If it does, the brush-size keys scale a 150-Awe meteor from the specified 0.05 rad crater to 0.14 rad, with "heavy damage to 2.5x" = 0.35 rad, at the same price. Hotkeys: Input handles "one letter per power" and HUD shows it on the button, but there is no table and no `key` field, and W A S D Q E R F H are taken. The two engineers will pick different letters, so the button advertises a key that arms another power.
issues.fix: Add `key` to the power definition in §3.10 and this rule: "`ang` passed to `Powers.use` is honoured only for brush powers and `seed` (clamped 0.025 to 0.14). Every other click power always uses its definition's `ang`." SPEC-UI §2: "The ring radius is `Game.brushAng` for brush powers and `seed`, otherwise `Powers.byId[id].ang`. Hotkeys come from `Powers.byId[id].key`; Input and HUD never define their own." Keys (binding): comet C, seed G, awaken K, raise T, lower Y, rain N, bloom B, lightning L, quake U, plague X, meteor M, volcano V, heal J, inspire I, prophet P, peace O.

issues.where: SPEC-UI §5 (`Screens.open`), §2 (Input: "Ignore input when ... a screen is open")
issues.problem: `Screens.close()        Screens.open -> name of the open screen or null` has no parentheses, so it reads as a property, while every other `->` in these documents is a function return. Input must test it. If Input writes `if (DM.Screens.open) return;` and Screens ships a function, the test is always truthy and the game accepts no input at all. If Input writes `DM.Screens.open()` and Screens ships a string, it throws inside `Input.update`, which is the first call in game.js's frame try block: everything after it, including `Renderer.frame`, is skipped every frame and the screen stays black.
issues.fix: Rename to `Screens.current` and state: "`Screens.current` is a property, never a function: 'title' | 'setup' | 'pause' | 'settings' | 'help' | 'ending' | 'timelapse' | 'card' | null." SPEC-UI §2: "Input ignores pointer and key input while `DM.Screens && DM.Screens.current` is truthy, and ignores keys while `document.activeElement` is an input or textarea."

issues.where: SPEC-SIM §3.3 (`Climate.emit`, `Climate.addDust`, yearly globals), §3.7 (factory), §3.8 (Awe income, nukes), §3.10 (costs, meteor/volcano dust), §4 (Awe target)
issues.problem: Three feedback loops are split between two authors with no agreed scale. CO2: Civ calls `Climate.emit(world, amount)` per factory, and Climate turns `co2` into `3 x log2(1 + co2/100)` and "relaxes toward 0 slowly". Neither the unit of `amount` nor the uptake rate is given, so the integrated result is either no warming or runaway, and the late-game climate arc is a pillar. Dust: `Climate.addDust` is called by Powers (meteor, ash) and Society (nukes) with no amounts, against -9 C per unit. Awe: Society's income is per sim year and linear in settlements. With 30 shrine settlements (devotion 0.5, mean tier 1.5) it is 0.6 + 30 x 0.5 x 0.7 x 1.75 = about 19 Awe/yr, i.e. 38 Awe per real second at 1x: a 150-Awe meteor every 4 seconds, where §4 wants a great miracle "every few minutes". Late game is worse. Powers owns the costs and cannot fix it.
issues.fix: Paste as starting values with the owner named. §3.7: "A settlement with a factory emits `0.6 x pop / 1e6` co2 units per year (x0.5 in the Space age)." §3.3: "Uptake is `0.5 % x (0.5 + mean veg)` of co2 per year. Target, verified in simrun and owned by the Climate author: an undisturbed world reaches co2 60 to 200 (globalTemp +2 to +4.5) by the Ark." Dust amounts: meteor +0.25, volcano +0.02 per year of eruption, each nuke +0.12. §3.8: "Income per year = `0.6 + 0.45 x sqrt(sum)`, with the sum as before" (one camp: about 0.7/yr; 30 shrine settlements: about 2.5/yr; 100 templed cities: about 6/yr). "The Society author owns the Awe target in §4 and may change income, never the costs in §3.10."

issues.where: SPEC-SIM §1 (Unit), §2 (`unit:*` rows), §3.8 (`Society.onArrive`, prophets), §3.9 (Units)

result.verdict: Not ready for a parallel build from the interface lens. There are two blockers: the genesis-to-history hand-off has no owner (no phase setter, and nobody writes `vars.seaBase` / `vars.iceRef`, so sea level goes NaN in the first year of history), and `world.rivers` has three different shapes across the documents. issues.where: SPEC-SIM.md §3.7 Civ: 'converts its best territory cells to farmland as it grows ... lets farms lapse when it shrinks', 'Growth: logistic toward K', 'above capacity people starve', Settlement.K 'computed last year'
issues.problem: Wrong-signed feedback and a numeric trap. If K is computed from the current farm[] and farms follow population, then a drought or fire that halves K starves people, farms lapse, K falls again, and the settlement spirals down to forager level or below 3 people after the first famine, even when the land has recovered. Separately, logistic growth r x P x (1 - P/K) divides by K: K is undefined in the founding year ('computed last year') and is 0 when the territory is burnt, flooded, lava-covered or entirely owned by neighbours, giving NaN or -Infinity population that then poisons stats.pop, culture.pop and science. The starvation rate is not specified at all, so two engineers will produce anything from a gentle decline to instant death.
issues.fix: Add: 'K is computed from potential yields (see Food) and never depends on farm[] or on the current population. After K is known, farm[] is set for display and ecology: the best cells by farmPot are farmed until their summed farmPot reaches 1.15 x pop; the others relax toward 0 by 0.1 per year.' 'Civ.found claims territory and computes K immediately. Keff = max(K, 1). If pop <= Keff: pop += r x pop x (1 - pop/Keff), r = 0.03 x (1 + 0.3 granary + 0.3 if blessed + 0.2 x max(0, love)), famine = 0. Else: pop -= min(0.12 x pop, 0.5 x (pop - Keff)), famine += 1 (settlement:famine when famine reaches 3). Then plague deaths. pop is clamped to >= 0 and the settlement is destroyed below 3.' With these numbers a halved K costs at most 12 % per year and the settlement stabilises at the new K instead of collapsing.

Fixed thresholds that put a 60-settlement single-culture world in the windows put a four-culture world 3-4x late (Space after year 6,000, no Ark by 4,500) and a large world early. Finally the yearly tick has unbounded path searches: every settlement near capacity runs a planet-wide naval Path.reach (up to 25 ms each), and with no rule that a failed search starts the cooldown, a full continent retries every year: 30 settlements = 750 ms in one tick.
issues.fix: Replace the tick-order tail with a one-stage-per-tick pipeline and add need.bio to FOUNDATION §5.2 (world.need = { hydro, climate, derive, bio }): 'Yearly work runs when (tick - vars.t0) % 4 === 0 (vars.t0 = tick at which history began), so it lands on whole years. stepIce runs when tick % 20 === 10. On every tick that is not a yearly tick, run at most ONE of, in this order: need.derive -> Terrain.derive; (need.climate and at least 8 ticks since the last climate pass) or 40 ticks since it -> Climate.update, which sets need.hydro and need.bio; need.hydro and at least 8 ticks since the last -> Hydro.update, which sets need.bio; need.bio -> Life.classify + Life.habitability.' 'Climate.yearly sets need.climate only when globalTemp - 9 x dust has changed by 0.25 C, or seaLevel by 0.03, since the last Climate.update.' 'Per yearly tick at most 2 expansion searches (longest-waiting settlement first, ties by id; Path.reach maxCost 45 on land, 120 naval) and at most 4 Units.spawn path searches for armies and traders; trade paths are cached per settlement pair in world._routes. Any expansion search, successful or not, sets lastExpand.'

issues.where: SPEC-SIM.md §3.10 Powers.update ('real-time pieces ... runs even while the sim is paused'; comet 1.4 s, meteor 1.6 s; data.eta in real seconds), §3.12 simrun / policies, SPEC-UI.md §0 debug.ff / debug.use; FOUNDATION.md §0 Determinism; SPEC-SIM §3.11 culture._seen
issues.problem: Comets and meteors only land inside Powers.update(realDt), which only the browser game loop calls. Sim.tick never calls it, so in tools/simrun.js the cruel and chaotic policies launch meteors that never arrive (the 'cruel player can drive a world to silence' target cannot be verified), debug.use followed by debug.ff never produces an impact, and a headless genesis cannot fill the sea with comets. In the browser the impact tick depends on frame timing and game speed (1.6 s is 13 ticks at 1x and 102 ticks = 25 years at 8x), so 'same seed + same inputs at the same ticks' does not hold unless the mapping is defined. Smaller divergence sources: render, audio and FX Bus handlers are not forbidden from drawing on world.rng (the headless run has no such handlers, so its stream differs); the 'at most 4 per real second' rate limits need a clock that sim files may not read; the per-culture witnessed-deeds record may live in culture._seen, which is transient and not rebuildable, so epithets change after a reload.
issues.fix: Add to §3.10: 'Flight time is counted only by the dt passed to Powers.update. Headless drivers (simrun, debug.ff, Sim.genesis.skip, tests) must call Powers.update(world, 0.125) once after every Sim.tick, which is the 1x mapping of 8 ticks per real second. Impacts are resolved inside Powers.update using world.rng. Real-second rate limits are measured by accumulating that dt, never a clock.' Add to FOUNDATION §0 Determinism: 'Only js/sim/* may draw from world.rng or any fork of it; render, audio, UI and FX use their own generators. Determinism is guaranteed for an uninterrupted run with the same sequence of Sim.tick, Powers.update and Powers.use calls; a save/load boundary may diverge because fields are quantized and derived fields are refreshed.' In §3.11 replace 'culture._seen or world.vars' with a persisted field 'culture.seen: { powerId: count }' and add it to the Culture shape in §1. Snapshots are due when year >= vars.snapNext, not on a modulo of a float year.

issues.where: SPEC-SIM.md §3.7 Expansion ('12 % of its people ... best reachable unclaimed site ... at least ~7 hops from any other territory. Cooldown 25 years'), Tier, Hazards ('population < 3 -> destroyed'); FOUNDATION §5.1 owner i16
issues.problem: Several holes that only show up when run forward. (1) A camp of 30 near its capacity sends 12 % = 3.6 people; Civ.found creates a settlement that dies at the next hazard check or the first bad year. Dead settlements are never removed, so churn of this kind (up to one founding per settlement per 25 years for 4,000 years) can push ids toward the i16 limit of owner and bloat every save. (2) Tier has no hysteresis: a village of 62 sends settlers, drops to 55, is demoted to camp, its radius shrinks 3 -> 2, K halves, people starve, then it regrows and is promoted again, emitting settlement:tier and chronicle lines each cycle. (3) A target site is not reserved, so during the 2-4 years a party walks, every neighbour picks the same best site, loses 12 % and gets nothing. (4) 'Near capacity' and the distance test (from territory, which needs a ring scan per candidate cell inside a Dijkstra flood) are undefined. For reference the rules as written give a settlement doubling time of about 70 years (130 years to mature, then one party per 30), so the home continent is full by year 500-700: fine for the 8-40 target, but only if these holes are closed.
issues.fix: Rewrite the Expansion bullet: 'A settlement with pop >= 0.85 K, pop >= 40 and year - lastExpand >= 25 (12 under the expand edict) may send settlers. Party size = clamp(0.12 x pop, 12, 500), removed from the origin. Candidate sites must have Civ.canSettle ok, an estimated camp K >= 60, be at least 7 hops from every owned cell (use world._ownDist, a multi-source BFS distance field capped at 8, rebuilt once per year) and at least 9 hops from the dest of any live settler unit. The best by siteScore minus 0.01 x path cost wins. If none exists, lastExpand = year - 15 (retry in 10 years).' Tier: 'Promote when pop reaches the gate; demote only when pop < 0.5 x the gate of the current tier.' Add: 'Civ.found returns null when there are 160 live settlements or world.settlements.length >= 30,000.' Territory: 'When two settlements re-claim in the same year, a contested unowned cell goes to the nearer centre (ties: lower id).'

issues.where: SPEC-SIM.md §3.8 Relations, war, battles, Atomic age, New cultures; §4 (living cultures at year 2,000: 2-6; passive worlds launch an Ark; no extinction on 9 of 10 seeds)
issues.problem: No numbers anywhere in the diplomacy loop, and several dead ends. (1) Wars may never start (baseline positive, trade improves) or never stop: 'ends by exhaustion' is undefined, and if exhaustion only rises from battles, two cultures separated by sea before the Sail age can never reach each other (Units.spawn returns null), so the war flag and trade ban last forever. (2) The battle formula compares an army's size with the defender's whole population times walls: an army of 6 % of a city can never beat a peer, so the '40 % of settlements lost' end condition is unreachable. Whether the army's people leave the source is unspecified. (3) Nuclear exchange has no probability; with 700-1,000 years spent in Atomic+ and a war per pair every couple of centuries, any per-year risk above a few percent makes an exchange near-certain in passive worlds, hitting the largest cities (the capitals building Arks) with a 9 C dust winter. (4) Culture splits have no thresholds; before Sail there is no 'overseas', so a compact home continent can still be one culture at year 2,000, missing the 2-6 target.
issues.fix: Add starting numbers to §3.8. Relations, yearly per pair in contact: 'v += 0.03 x (0.1 - v) + 0.04 x trade - 0.02 x border - 0.03 x max(0, aggrA + aggrB - 0.9) - 0.03 x |loveA - loveB| + 0.03 x rng.gauss(), clamped to -1..1. War when v < -0.5, year >= truce and the more aggressive side has at least 0.6 of the other's population x tech.' War: 'exhaustion += 0.015 per year at war, + 0.08 per lost battle, + 0.15 per settlement lost; peace when either side reaches 1, after 60 years regardless, or at 40 % settlements lost; then v = -0.1, truce = year + 40, exhaustion decays 0.03 per year. Each side sends one army every 8 years from its largest settlement within path cost 60 of an enemy settlement: size = 6 % of that settlement's people (removed). Battle: size x tech[a] x rng.range(0.7, 1.3) versus 0.05 x pop x (1 + walls) x tech[d], tech = [1, 1.5, 2.2, 3, 5, 8, 10]; win -> capture (raze if pop < 100) and the defender loses 15 %; lose -> army dies.' Nuclear: '1.5 % per year per warring pair with both sides Atomic+; at most one exchange per war: 2 strikes per side on the largest cities (30 % survive, rad 0.8 within 2 hops, dust per the climate table), then immediate peace with a 100-year truce.' Splits: 'A settlement is estranged while it is more than 30 hops (0.57 rad) from its capital or on another landmass, or its love differs from the culture mean by more than 0.6; after 120 consecutive estranged years (persist as s.apart) two or more estranged settlements within 15 hops of each other secede together. At most one birth per parent per 150 years; at most 6 living cultures.'

issues.where: SPEC-SIM.md §3.5 Fire ('spreads to neighbours with probability rising with their vegetation and dryness'), §3.10 Powers.natural ('wildfire lightning', droughts, quakes, eruptions, plague), §4 (no extinction on 9 of 10 seeds)
issues.problem: Fire on this grid is a percolation process with a sharp threshold. The cell graph is a triangular lattice (6 neighbours), whose bond-percolation threshold is 0.347: if a burning cell's lifetime chance of igniting a given neighbour is above about 0.35, one strike burns the entire connected forest; below it, fires stay small. With no number given, the life author lands on one side or the other by accident: either lightning is cosmetic, or every natural strike strips a continent of the veg and fauna that Stone-age foraging lives on. This matters most in the first 130 years, when the whole species is a single camp of 30-150 people. One natural fire, quake (15-35 %), eruption or drought on that one camp ends the game, and Powers.natural rolls every year with no rates given. Hitting 9 of 10 seeds needs this to be bounded by rule, not luck.
issues.fix: Add to §3.5 Fire: 'A cell burns for exactly 2 ticks and makes one ignition attempt per neighbour, on its first tick, with P = 0.55 x veg x dry, dry = sat(1.2 - 1.6 x (moist + wet)); never onto sea, ice, lake, or veg < 0.15. (Wet forest P < 0.05; dry savanna and forest about 0.28, sub-critical; only drought on dense vegetation exceeds 0.35.) No new ignitions while world._fires holds more than 1,500 cells. Burning removes 80 % of veg and sets scorch.' Add to §3.10: 'Natural events per century at calamity 1: lightning fires 6, storms 3, droughts 2, quakes 1, plague 1 (only where a city exists), eruptions 0.4; a drought lasts 6-12 years. While the world has fewer than 4 live settlements, or before year 150, no natural event is centred within 0.15 rad of a settlement.' Add simrun output: largest single fire (cells) and count of extinctions before year 300 over 10 seeds.

issues.where: SPEC-SIM.md §3.4 Hydro (lakes: 'water = filled - elev where that exceeds 0.03, capped at 2.5'), §3.5 Habitability and capacity, §3.6 Path, §3.7 Territory / Hazards / 'ruins that decay slowly'; FOUNDATION §5.1 farm, urban, owner
issues.problem: Lake cells have no rules outside hydro. They are land by definition, so they are habitable, farmable, claimable, walkable, plantable and valid settlement sites; a lake that forms under a town (after a crater, a lowered basin, or Terrain.roughen, which makes many one-cell pits per quake) drowns nothing while the renderer draws water over the houses. Priority-flood also turns every one-cell pit in the noise into a lake, so fresh water is within 2 hops of almost everything and 'a desert made liveable by fresh water' applies everywhere. Related state is never cleaned up: when a settlement dies its cells become unowned but nobody decays farm[] or urban[] (Civ only visits live settlements), and vegetation capacity is multiplied by (1 - farm), so abandoned farmland is bare forever. Cells that flood when the sea rises keep owner, farm, veg, road and lake water.
issues.fix: Add to §3.4: 'A depression becomes a lake only if it has at least 3 cells or a maximum depth of 0.25; smaller ones are treated as filled ground (water = 0) and drain through. A lake cell is a land cell with water > 0.03.' Add one line to each consumer: Life: 'capacity and hab are 0 on lake cells; on any cell with owner = -1, farm decays 5 % per year and urban 1 % per year; on sea cells veg, farm, urban, road, water, fire and scorch are set to 0 (fauna and ice keep their sea meaning).' Path: 'a lake step costs +2 on foot.' Civ: 'lake cells are never farmed and are not valid sites (canSettle reason 'sea'); a centre cell with water > 0.3 is destroyed as 'drowned'; claim drops sea cells.' Objects (SPEC-RENDER §9): 'no trees on lake cells.'

issues.where: SPEC-SIM.md §3.7 Civ.bestSite / Expansion ('naval from the Sail age if it has a port'), §3.6 Path naval, §3.10 awaken; CONCEPT 'choose where the first tribe wakes'
issues.problem: Expansion can simply never happen. Nothing crosses water before Sail (year 1,200-2,000). If the first tribe wakes on an island or a small continent (the player may choose it, and bestSite ranks single cells by habitability with no regard for how much land is around them), the world holds 1-6 settlements for a millennium and a half; science then crawls, Sail arrives late or never, and the Ark window is missed while nothing visibly changes for 20 minutes of play. Even on a good continent the map is static from about year 600 (continent full) until Sail. 'Overseas' in the culture-split rule also needs a landmass test that no module provides except by running Path.find.
issues.fix: Add to §3.2 Terrain.derive: 'also labels connected land components into world._landId (Int16Array, -1 on sea) and world._landHab (habitable cell count per component).' Change §3.7: 'Civ.bestSite only considers cells on the landmass with the largest _landHab (falling back to any land).' Change §3.10 awaken: 'Powers.can returns { ok: true, reason: 'small' } when the target landmass has fewer than 600 habitable cells, so the HUD can warn.' Change §3.6: 'naval is false | 'coastal' | true. 'coastal' allows sea steps only on cells shallower than 0.6 (SHALLOWS), cost 0.6 each.' Change Expansion: 'from the Bronze age a settlement with a sea cell in its territory searches with naval = 'coastal' (canoes along shelves and between near islands); from the Sail age with a port, naval = true.'

issues.where: SPEC-SIM.md §3.3 Moisture ('normalized annual rainfall 0..1 plus wet[c], minus 0.25 inside active droughts'), §3.4 runoff = moist + wet, §3.3 Temperature ('sea cells never below -2') versus Ice ('sea ice where a sea cell is below about -2.5'), milestones (globalTemp <= -2, -4), §3.5 Vegetation / Life.step, §3.12 'life' phase
issues.problem: A cluster of small contradictions, each inside one or two modules. (1) wet is counted twice in river runoff, and moist only changes when Climate.update runs (every 10 years), so a rain miracle or a 6-year drought has no effect unless someone sets need.climate at its start and end; nobody is told to. (2) 'Normalized' rainfall is ambiguous: normalizing by the planet's current maximum means one new mountain dries the whole world. (3) Sea temperature is clamped at -2 but sea ice needs below -2.5, so SEAICE can never form. (4) Cooling milestones use globalTemp, which is driven only by co2 >= 0, so 'cooling' and 'ice-age' can never fire and the HUD anomaly ignores a nuclear winter. (5) Life.step is not told its time step; treating a call as one tick instead of parts x TICK makes regrowth 8x slow. (6) The green wave can advance at most one hop per visit of a cell (one visit per real second at parts = 8), so 20-30 s per continent is at the edge of possible; and because vegetation 'never appears from nothing', any landmass the player did not touch stays bare for the whole game.
issues.fix: Paste: (1) 'Hydro runoff = moist[c]. Powers sets need.climate when a drought starts or ends and when the rain brush or a tsunami has raised wet (the scheduler rate-limits it).' (2) 'moist = sat(rain / RAIN_REF) with a fixed constant chosen so a wet equatorial coast is about 0.9.' (3) 'Sea ice equilibrium uses the unclamped sea temperature: 0 at -2.5 ramping to 1 at -6.' (4) 'Climate.anomaly(world) = globalTemp - 9 x dust; milestones and the HUD use it.' (5) 'Each Life.step call advances its cells by dt = parts x Sim.TICK years.' (6) 'In the life phase Sim calls Life.step(tick % 2, 2). While Life.cover(world).veg > 0.1, an empty plantable cell sprouts (veg = 0.02) with probability 0.0003 per year.'

result.verdict: Not ready from the simulation-dynamics lens: the module APIs and event list are sound, but the rules that decide how a world actually unfolds are either missing a number, missing an owner, or (in four places) contradict each other. Two items will break integration outright (climate datum and seaBase/iceRef initialisation; who sets and repairs a culture's capital and declares it dead), and the cross-module quantities (K per cell, science pacing, Awe income, witness units, CO2 and dust amounts, sea-level amplitude) are set by engineers who cannot talk, so the first assembled world will either stall, peg, or drown. Every fix above is a paste-in sentence or number rather than a restructuring; with them merged into SPEC-SIM.md (plus need.bio and the determinism lines in FOUNDATION.md) the documents are fit for a parallel build, with the caveat that my numbers are hand-derived estimates, not simulated, and still need a simrun pass on several seeds.

issues.where: SPEC-RENDER §1 `GL.frame`, §2 Frame block (`uFx`, `uWorld`, `uPlanet`, `uTime`, `uViewProj`), §6 `Planet.setOverlay`, §7 `Sky.update`
issues.problem: `frame.set(name, x, y, z, w)` writes a whole vec4, but several vec4s have split owners. `uFx` = cloud opacity (camera-dependent, owner unnamed) + cloudiness and ocean fraction (Sky.update). `uWorld` = heat and dust (world), night-light level (owner unnamed), overlay mode (Planet.setOverlay). `uTime.z` is cloud drift. `uPlanet.z/.w` are shell radii whose values appear nowhere in any document. Whoever writes last zeroes the other's components (clouds at radius 0, overlay reset every frame). Nobody is named as the caller of `upload()`, although the block must be uploaded twice per frame because `uViewProj` is the light matrix during the shadow pass. A renderer that uploads once, or a module that uploads from its own sync, renders the shadow map with the camera matrix.
issues.fix: Add `frame.setc(name, i, value)` (one component) to §1 and this paragraph to §2: "Only renderer.js calls `frame.upload()`: once after step 1 with uViewProj = light matrix, once before the scene pass with uViewProj = camera. Writers: renderer.js writes all matrices, uCamPos, uSunDir, uSunCol, uTime.x/y/w, uScreen, uPlanet (x = DM.R, y = displayed sea level, z = GL.CLOUD_R, w = GL.ATMO_R), uBrush, uBrushCol, uFlash, uFlashCol, uWorld.x/y (heat, dust), uWorld.z = [0.12, 0.2, 0.35, 0.5, 0.8, 1, 1][world.age], uWorld.w = Planet's current overlay mode. Sky.update writes, with setc only: uFx.x (cloud opacity = smoothstep(14, 40, altitude)), uFx.y, uFx.z, uTime.z, and uStorms. No other module writes the frame." Add constants to gl.js: `GL.CLOUD_R = DM.R + 11`, `GL.ATMO_R = DM.R + 17`.

issues.where: SPEC-RENDER §1 `GL.program` (uShadowMap on unit 7), §3 `<lighting>`, §4 step 2 (shadow pass), §6 and §9 `drawDepth`
issues.problem: Nobody is assigned to bind the shadow texture to unit 7, and nothing says how depth-pass programs differ from colour programs. "Colour writes off, polygon offset on" plus Objects' "one shared instanced program" invites reusing the colour program in drawDepth. That program has an active `uShadowMap` sampler on unit 7 while the same texture is the draw framebuffer's depth attachment: WebGL2 raises INVALID_OPERATION (rendering feedback loop) on every draw, so the shadow map stays empty and the console floods. In the other direction, if unit 7 has no texture (first frame, shadows off at quality 0, dev viewer) every `sunShadow` returns 0 and the planet is black. Polygon-offset values and who sets pass state are unspecified, and a drawDepth that obeys §4 literally ("colour mask all true" on exit) undoes the pass state.
issues.fix: Add to §4: "Shadow contract. renderer.js owns the shadow target and is the only code that touches texture unit 7: `GL.bindTex(7, null)` before the shadow pass, `GL.bindTex(7, shadow.depthTex)` before the scene pass. Units 6 and 7 are reserved; modules use 0-5. Every `drawDepth()` uses a dedicated depth program: the same vertex position code as the colour program (yaw, sway, far-side cull), fragment body `void main(){}`, and it must not include `<lighting>` or `<clouds>`. For the shadow pass the renderer sets colorMask(false x4), POLYGON_OFFSET_FILL with polygonOffset(1.5, 4.0), cull off, and clears depth; drawDepth must not change colour mask, polygon offset or cull. When shadows are off the renderer binds a 1x1 depth texture cleared to 1.0 to unit 7 and sets uShadowMat so every point maps to (0.5, 0.5, 0)." Add to §1: "The shadow depth texture is DEPTH_COMPONENT24 with TEXTURE_COMPARE_MODE = COMPARE_REF_TO_TEXTURE, COMPARE_FUNC = LEQUAL, LINEAR filtering, CLAMP_TO_EDGE. `sunShadow` returns 1 when the shadow coordinate is outside 0..1 and fades to 1 over the outer 8 % of the map."

issues.where: FOUNDATION §5.2 `world.rivers`; SPEC-SIM §3.4 `Hydro.update`; SPEC-RENDER §6 (rivers) and §11 `DM.Fixtures`
issues.problem: FOUNDATION says `world.rivers` is an "array of Int32Array cell polylines". SPEC-SIM §3.4 says it is an array of `{ cells: Int32Array, flow: Float32Array }`. The Planet ribbon builder ("width from flow") and Fixtures are written from RENDER + FOUNDATION, Hydro from SPEC-SIM. One side will index `river[i]`, the other `river.cells[i]`; rivers either vanish silently or Planet.sync throws inside the frame loop every time `dirty.rivers` is set. It is also unstated whether the last point is the sea or lake cell, so ribbons may stop up to one cell (1.9 units) short of the shore.
issues.fix: Change FOUNDATION §5.2 to: "`world.rivers = []` derived: array of `{ cells: Int32Array, flow: Float32Array }` (equal length; `flow[i]` = discharge at `cells[i]`), ordered source to mouth. The last cell is the first sea cell, the first lake cell, or the confluence cell (inclusive), so a ribbon always ends under a water surface or on another river." Repeat the same sentence in SPEC-SIM §3.4 and SPEC-RENDER §6; state in §11 that Fixtures produces this shape.

issues.where: SPEC-RENDER §9 `Objects.sync`, §6 `Planet.groundAt` / `surfaceAt`, §4 step 1; SPEC-SIM §0.7 `dirty.objects`, §3.2 `Terrain.touched`, §3.5 `Life.classify`
issues.problem: (a) Cost. `dirty.objects` is one global boolean and the sim sets it almost continuously during history (vegetation crossing thresholds on every Life.step, 25-120 settlements changing). Each time, Objects rebuilds every tree on the planet: about 16,000 land cells x 1-3 trees = 15-30 k `Planet.groundAt` calls, each a hint-less `geo.cellAt` (up to 10 us) plus a barycentric lookup, i.e. roughly 50-300 ms, allowed at 2 Hz. That is a visible hitch twice a second for the whole game. The ~300 movers plus decorative life call `surfaceAt` every frame, another 1-4 ms without a hint. (b) Correctness. `Terrain.touched` sets dirty.elev/water/color but not dirty.objects, and Planet.sync clears dirty.elev before Objects.sync runs. Objects are only re-grounded through the parenthetical "(+ dirty.objects)" in Life.classify on a later tick. While paused (meteor impacts resolve in real time even when paused) trees and houses hang in the air over the new crater until the sim resumes.
issues.fix: SPEC-SIM §3.2: "`Terrain.touched` also sets `dirty.objects`." §3.3: "A sea-level change that sets dirty.water also sets dirty.objects." SPEC-RENDER §6: "`Planet.groundAt(dir, hint = -1)`, `Planet.surfaceAt(dir, hint = -1)`: hint is a cell id near dir (the cell being populated, or the unit's current cell from Units.dirOf)." §9: "Objects.sync never rebuilds the planet's trees in one frame. Trees are re-instanced by a rolling sweep over cells (at least 500 cells per frame, at most 1.5 ms, whole planet in about 1.5 s) into a back buffer that is swapped in when the sweep completes. dirty.objects only (re)starts a sweep and is cleared immediately. Each settlement keeps its own instance range and is rebuilt individually on `settlement:founded | tier | building | destroyed | captured` and whenever a sweep passes its cell. Movers pass their current cell as the hint."

issues.where: SPEC-RENDER §0 (budget line), §8 (model triangle limits), §9 (trees "1-3 per cell", settlements, far-side cull); SPEC-SIM §4 (25-120 settlements, 1-10 M people)
issues.problem: The numbers do not add up. Trees: about 9-10 k vegetated cells x up to 3 x "under ~40 triangles" is about 1.1 M triangles. Late-game settlements (mostly cities and metropolises when the world holds 1-10 M people) x hundreds of houses x "under ~150 triangles" is another 1-2 M. All of it is drawn twice (scene + shadow), and because culling happens in the vertex shader every instance on the planet is vertex-shaded in both passes at every zoom. That is 3-5 M triangles against a stated 1.2 M; 45 models x 2 passes is already 90 draw calls against "about 60". Each engineer will cut differently. Separately, a naive far-side cull (`dot(dir, camDir) < R/d`) removes mountain-top trees that are still above the horizon at close zoom and casters that still shadow the terminator.
issues.fix: Replace the budget line in §0 with: "Budget at quality 2: scene pass at most 1.2 M triangles, shadow pass at most 1.0 M, at most 150 draw calls." §8: "Trees, shrub, cactus, rock: at most 20 triangles. Homes: at most 48. Civic and movers: at most 150." §9: "Instance caps for quality 0 / 1 / 2: trees 6,000 / 14,000 / 24,000 (thin deterministically by cell hash when over). Building instances 2,500 / 5,000 / 8,000 planet-wide; per settlement at most 6 / 14 / 40 / 110 / 260 by tier, scaled down uniformly when the planet-wide cap is reached. `Objects.drawDepth()` draws nothing when `GL.view.zoom01 < 0.3` (a tree is under 5 px there) and nothing at quality 0. Far-side cull, both passes: hide an instance only when angle(instance direction, camera direction) > acos(p/|cam|) + acos(p/|pos|) + 0.05, with p = uPlanet.x + min(uPlanet.y, 0.0) - 1.0."

issues.where: SPEC-RENDER §0 Look, §6 Terrain, §8 Models, §9 trees; SPEC-UI §1 (altitude 6 at zoom 1)
issues.problem: This is the decision most likely to make the game look cheap. A cell is 1.9 units and the only terrain signal is one interpolated vertex colour per cell. At zoom 1 (eye about 11 units from the focus, fov 35 deg, 1080p) one unit is about 150 px, so the near field is a few dozen triangles, each roughly 300 px of linear colour gradient with one flat normal, with 45 px houses standing on them. Biome borders are straight 300 px gradients. Forests are "1-3 trees per cell": three crowns about 0.4 wide on 3 square units is roughly 12-15 % cover, an orchard of lollipops rather than a canopy. Houses with a radial up axis float on their downhill side on any slope. The pillar "seamless zoom from orbit down to individual houses" depends on exactly this view.
issues.fix: Add to §6 Terrain: "Fragment detail is binding, not optional. Using `<noise>` on world position: albedo variation of +/-12 % at three scales (about 6, 1 and 0.15 units); a detail normal from the noise gradient whose strength rises with `uScreen.z`; biome borders broken up by perturbing the interpolated vertex colour with noise so they are ragged, not linear; steep facets (face normal against the radial up) shift toward rock; grass, sand and snow each get their own fine pattern. All detail fades out below zoom01 = 0.3 so it cannot alias from orbit." Add to §8: "Every model extends 0.15 below y = 0 (foundation or trunk) so it never floats on a slope. Add `grove_broadleaf, grove_conifer, grove_jungle`: 3-4 trunks in one mesh, footprint about 1 unit, at most 40 triangles." Add to §9: "Cells with veg > 0.6 in FOREST, RAINFOREST or TAIGA use grove models so three instances close the canopy." Add to §6: "Ground colour under vegetation darkens with veg so the forest reads from orbit without the trees."

issues.where: SPEC-RENDER §4 step 1, §7 `Sky.update(dt, world)`, §9 `Objects.sync(world, dt)`, §10 `FX.update(dt, world)` and `FX.spawn`; SPEC-SIM §3.5 `world._fires`, §1 `Disaster`
issues.problem: The per-frame update functions receive no camera and no quality level, yet the spec asks FX for effects "by world state near the camera" and "campfire smoke at close zoom", Sky for opacity that "fades out as the camera descends", and Objects for "villagers (close zoom only)" and tree density "by quality". issues.fix: Add to §1: "`GL.view`: set by Renderer.frame before step 1; the Camera.view() object plus `viewProj` (Float32Array(16)), `aspect` and `focusDir` (unit). `GL.quality`: 0 | 1 | 2. Any render module may read both; treat a null view as far orbit." SPEC-SIM §3.5: "`world._fires = { cells: Int32Array, n }`; the burning cells are `cells[0 .. n-1]`." issues.where: SPEC-RENDER §4 step 2 ("orthographic box fitted around what the camera can see"), §1 `GL.depthTarget(size)`, §2 `uShadowMat`, §3 `sunShadow`
issues.problem: The fit is not defined, and the literal reading fails where it matters. At zoom 1 the camera (altitude 6, tilt 58 deg) sees to the horizon 35-80 units away. A box around all of that on a 2048 map is about 0.04 units per texel while the screen shows about 150 px per unit: one shadow texel covers 6 px and a 0.3-unit house casts a shadow 7 texels wide. "Crisp sun shadows" fails exactly where the diorama is inspected. Also unspecified: the map size; that casters outside the view frustum (a mountain behind the camera near the terminator) must still be inside the box; texel snapping, without which every shadow edge crawls when the camera moves; and how grazing-angle acne at the terminator is handled on a sphere where a whole band of terrain is nearly parallel to the light.
issues.fix: Replace the last sentence of step 2 with: "Fit: centre c = `GL.view.target`; radius r = clamp(1.6 x |eye - target|, 12, DM.R + 22). Light space: z along uSunDir, x and y from a basis built from world +Y (from +X when the sun is within 5 deg of a pole). The ortho box is [c.x - r, c.x + r] x [c.y - r, c.y + r] with c.x and c.y snapped to multiples of 2r / size. The z range always spans the whole planet (from -(DM.R + 22) to +(DM.R + 22) measured from the planet centre), so every caster between the sun and the box is included. Map size for quality 0 / 1 / 2: 1024 / 2048 / 4096 (2048 when `caps.maxTex` < 8192). Above an eye-to-target distance of 76 the box is the whole planet. `sunShadow` offsets the lookup along the normal by 1.5 texels (texel size in world units is derivable from uShadowMat) and `shade` multiplies the result into N.L, so acne at the terminator is hidden by the lighting falloff."

issues.where: SPEC-RENDER §0 ("Sun-lit white about 2.5; emissive about 3-10"), §5 Post ("threshold about 1.2", `exposure: 1`)
issues.problem: The three numbers contradict each other, and every module author will shade against them. With sun-lit white at 2.5 and a bloom threshold of 1.2, every sun-lit surface with albedo above 0.48 blooms: ice caps, clouds, beaches, deserts, foam. The day side gets a permanent milky glow, and emissives at 3-10 barely separate from snow at 2.1. With exposure 1 through an ACES curve, a mid albedo of 0.3 x 2.5 = 0.75 lands at about 87 % display brightness after gamma, so the "saturated biome colours" are pushed into the shoulder and come out pastel. Emitters are also sub-pixel from orbit (a window is about 0.05 units; a pixel is 0.19 units at zoom 0), so after the MSAA resolve "3-10" averages to nothing and night cities will not glitter.
issues.fix: Replace those lines with a binding calibration block in §0: "Albedos are linear and at most 0.85 (snow and cloud 0.85, sand 0.45, grass 0.10-0.18, deep water 0.03). Sun-lit white = 2.5 scene units. `Post.set.exposure` defaults to 0.6. Bloom uses a soft-knee threshold of 3.0 scene units (knee 1.0): nothing diffuse blooms; only emissive surfaces, specular glint and the sun do. Emissive scale: lava and fire 4-8; windows and the terrain's urban night lights 8-20 (they are sub-pixel from orbit); lightning and impact flashes 20-40; the sun disc 40." §5: "Bloom: soft-knee threshold 3.0; clamp the bloom input to 64 to stop fireflies; 4-5 level down/up chain." Change `Post.set` default to `exposure: 0.6`.

issues.where: SPEC-RENDER §3 `atmosphere()` (gl.js author), §7 `Sky.drawAtmosphere` and `Sky.drawClouds` (sky author), §4 steps 3.5-3.6
issues.problem: Two different engineers each implement half of one effect. `atmosphere()` adds haze "toward the limb" on every surface; `drawAtmosphere` is an "additive halo; depth test on", which for a shell mesh also covers the whole planet disc. Either the disc gets haze twice, or the two halves disagree in colour and intensity at the silhouette and the planet shows a dark outline or a bright step exactly on its edge, which is the first thing the eye lands on in every orbit screenshot. The cloud shell has the same class of problem: with cull face off, its far-side back faces show in the ring between the planet's limb and the shell's limb, blended twice in arbitrary order.
issues.fix: Add to §3 `<lighting>`: "`vec3 inscatter(vec3 rayOrigin, vec3 rayDir, float tMax)`: sunlight scattered into a view ray over [0, tMax] inside the shell of radius `uPlanet.w` (blue by day, orange near the terminator, faint at night, scaled by `uFx.z`). `atmosphere(color, worldPos)` is defined as color x transmittance + inscatter(uCamPos.xyz, dir, distance to worldPos)." Change §7: "`Sky.drawAtmosphere` draws the shell sphere at `GL.ATMO_R` with FRONT faces culled and outputs inscatter(camera, dir, distance to the shell's far side). With depth test on it is therefore visible only outside the planet's silhouette, and it matches `atmosphere()` at the limb by construction. Haze over the disc comes only from `atmosphere()`. `Sky.drawClouds` passes its colour through `atmosphere()` and culls BACK faces when the camera is outside the cloud shell, FRONT faces when inside."

issues.where: SPEC-RENDER §4 steps 3.5-3.7, §10 `FX.draw`, §3 `<lighting>`
issues.problem: All particles are drawn after the cloud shell and are tested only against opaque depth. From orbit, everything below the cloud layer (forest-fire smoke, rain streaks, battle puffs, quake dust at radius about 101) is painted on top of clouds at radius about 111 that should hide it: rain appears in front of its own storm. Moving FX before the clouds breaks the opposite case (meteor trails, eruption columns, mushroom caps and the Ark plume above the clouds). Separately, "soft additive and soft alpha variants" drawn as two batches cannot interleave, so smoke is always entirely over or entirely under fire, and nothing makes unlit particles follow day and night, so grey smoke glows on the night side.
issues.fix: Change §4 step 3 to: "... 4. `Planet.drawWater()`; 5. `FX.draw(0)`: particles whose radius is below `GL.CLOUD_R`; 6. `Sky.drawClouds()`; 7. `Sky.drawAtmosphere()`; 8. `FX.draw(1)`: particles at or above `GL.CLOUD_R`, plus bolts, trails and rings." §10: "`FX.draw(layer)`. A particle's layer is decided each frame from its radius. All FX fragments output premultiplied alpha under one blend state, `blendFunc(ONE, ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA)` (additive = alpha 0), so one instanced draw per layer holds both kinds in spawn order. Non-emissive particles multiply their colour by `lightAt(worldPos)`." §3: "`vec3 lightAt(vec3 worldPos)`: unshadowed light for volumes = sun colour x dayAt x cloudShade + night ambient + the uFlash light. Used by particles and by the cloud shell."

issues.where: SPEC-UI §1 `Camera.update`, `Camera.view` (altitude 320 to 6, fov 35 deg, "near/far adapt to altitude"); SPEC-RENDER §0 ("terrain -6.5 ... +8.5"), §11 `Renderer.frame`; FOUNDATION §5.3 `ELEV_MAX = 20`
issues.problem: (a) Portrait. The 35 deg fov is vertical. At 390x844 the horizontal half-angle is atan(tan 17.5 deg x 0.462) = 8.3 deg, but the planet subtends 13.8 deg from altitude 320: at zoom 0 a phone shows a cropped middle strip and never the whole world. (b) "near/far adapt to altitude" has no numbers and is written by a UI engineer who does not know the cloud and atmosphere shells exist. A far plane at the terrain horizon clips the halo and clouds at close zoom; a fixed small near (say 0.1) at orbit gives about 0.1 units of depth resolution at 400 units, and the shoreline, lakes, rivers and roads (offsets of 0.02-0.05) z-fight. With an adaptive near, 24-bit depth is comfortable at every zoom, so this is purely a contract gap. (c) Render assumes terrain tops out at +8.5, but sculpting and volcano cones clamp at ELEV_MAX = 20, and "altitude 6 above the datum" is inside any mountain higher than +6.
issues.fix: SPEC-UI §1: "`Camera.update(dt, groundAt, aspect = 16/9)`; `Camera.view()` also returns `aspect`. Distance from the planet centre at zoom 0 = 1.08 x (DM.R + 17) / sin(atan(tan(fov/2) x min(1, aspect))), which is 420 in landscape and about 880 on a 390x844 phone. At zoom 1 the eye is 6 units above `groundAt` under the eye, not above the datum, and it stays at least 1.5 above the ground everywhere. `near = clamp(0.05 x height of the eye above the ground, 0.25, 150)`. `far = sqrt(d*d - 93*93) + 75` with d = |eye|, which reaches the far limb of the atmosphere shell." SPEC-RENDER §0: "Typical terrain is -6.5 ... +8.5 but may reach +20; peaks above `GL.CLOUD_R` rise through the clouds by design. The shadow box and all bounds use DM.R + 22. Ribbon and shoreline offsets rely on the near rule in SPEC-UI §1."

issues.where: SPEC-RENDER §6 `Planet.showSnapshot`; SPEC-UI §5 `Screens.timelapse`; SPEC-SIM §3.11 snapshot shape
issues.problem: Only Planet knows about snapshots. During the finale the terrain is recoloured to year 0 while Objects still draws today's forests, cities, ports and rocket; the night side still glitters at the final age; FX keeps smoking; the ocean stays at today's level (the snapshot's `seaLevel` has no consumer); and `Planet.sync` overwrites the snapshot colours the next time `dirty.color` is set (the sim "keeps working if ticked" in 'ended'). The player will watch Stone Age continents covered in tower blocks. The scale of the snapshot's `urban: Uint8Array` is also not stated.

It calls `Planet.showSnapshot(snap)` and `Objects.showSnapshot(snap)`, sets `uPlanet.y = snap.seaLevel`, sets `uWorld.z` from the fraction of land cells with `snap.urban > 0`, and skips FX.update and FX.draw while a snapshot is shown." §6: "While a snapshot is shown, Planet.sync leaves every dirty flag set and touches nothing. Colour = biome base colour (snapshots carry no vegetation), blended toward the owning culture's colour where `owner >= 0`, grey where `urban > 0`. `showSnapshot(null)` restores live colours and forces a full rebuild." §9: "`Objects.showSnapshot(snap | null)`: hide all trees, buildings and movers; draw one culture-tinted marker (`hut` where urban < 128, `townhouse` otherwise) on each cell with `snap.urban > 0`, at most 2,000; `null` restores." SPEC-SIM §3.11: "snapshot `urban` = round(urban x 255)."

issues.where: SPEC-RENDER §0 (performance targets), §3 `shade` / `cloudShade` / `cloudCover`, §5 `Post.resize(w, h, quality)`, §11 `Renderer.setQuality`, `Renderer.resize`
issues.problem: "Quality 0 | 1 | 2" changes behaviour in six modules, but only two effects are pinned down (MSAA at quality >= 1, tree count "by quality"). Six engineers will pick six meanings, and quality 0 will not be usable on integrated graphics: every lit fragment runs `shade` = PCF shadow + `cloudShade` (procedural 3D fbm, up to 40 hash evaluations for fbm5) + `atmosphere`, on the terrain, again on the water over it, and then the cloud shell runs fbm5 full-screen. Phones add three failures: devicePixelRatio 3 (a 4x MSAA RGBA16F + depth target at 1170x2532 is about 140 MB); GL context loss when the tab is backgrounded, for which the spec has no restore path (black canvas on return); and about 20 programs, each including `<lighting>`, compiled on first use, which is seconds of stall under ANGLE/D3D.
issues.fix: Add a binding table to §0, values for quality 0 / 1 / 2: pixel-ratio cap 1.0 / 1.5 / 2.0 and at most 1.6 / 3 / 5 megapixels (scale the drawing buffer down, CSS size unchanged); MSAA off plus FXAA in the final Post pass / 4x / 4x; shadow map 1024 terrain-only with 1 hardware-PCF tap / 2048 with 4 taps / 4096 with 9 taps; `cloudCover` octaves 3 / 5 / 5, and `cloudShade` never more than 3 octaves; bloom levels 3 / 5 / 5; tilt-shift off / on / on; particle cap 2,000 / 4,000 / 6,000; tree and building caps as in §9. Add: "Shaders branch on `uScreen.w`; CPU code reads `GL.quality`; `Renderer.setQuality` sets dirty.objects. If the 2-second mean of `Renderer.stats.ms` exceeds 26, the renderer drops one quality level (once per level) and emits `ui:toast`. The renderer handles `webglcontextlost` (preventDefault, stop drawing) and `webglcontextrestored` (GL.init, every module's init(), then setWorld(world)); every module's init() must be callable twice. Renderer.init creates every program before the first frame."

issues.where: SPEC-RENDER §4 (GL state rule), §1 `GL.mesh`, `GL.instances`
issues.problem: "Leave GL state as it found it" for five flags is not enough to stop eight independently written modules corrupting each other, and state cannot be cheaply read back in WebGL anyway. Not covered: the bound VAO (the ELEMENT_ARRAY_BUFFER binding is VAO state, so a `mesh.setIndex` or any index upload while another module's VAO is still bound silently rewires that VAO's indices: the terrain turns into spikes after a river rebuild); polygon offset (rivers and roads will enable it); cull mode and front face; depth func; scissor; blend func. The constants for disabled attributes ("normal (0,1,0), colour (1,1,1,1)") are context state, not VAO state, so they leak from one mesh to the next unless set at draw time.
issues.fix: Replace the rule with: "Canonical state on entry to and exit from every draw function: DEPTH_TEST on, depthFunc(LEQUAL), depthMask(true), BLEND off, CULL_FACE off with cullFace(BACK) and frontFace(CCW), SCISSOR_TEST off, no VAO bound, and colour mask and POLYGON_OFFSET_FILL as the renderer set them for the pass (a scene-pass draw that enables polygon offset disables it again). Whoever enables BLEND sets blendFunc first. Only `target.bind()` and `GL.toScreen()` change the framebuffer and viewport. The gl.js helpers bind their own VAO for every draw and every buffer operation and call `bindVertexArray(null)` afterwards; `mesh.draw()` and `inst.draw()` call `vertexAttrib4f` for each disabled attribute on every draw. The renderer re-asserts the canonical state before each numbered step of §4."

issues.where: SPEC-RENDER §6 Ocean, Lakes, rivers, roads, brush ring; §4 step 3.4 ("depth write on")
issues.problem: Four details will be built wrong as written. (1) "The same triangles on a sphere at DM.R + seaLevel" with per-vertex depth "seaLevel - elev" bakes sea level into two vertex buffers, so every comet step and every climate change forces a 40,962-vertex rebuild and the sea jumps instead of rising. (2) "Lakes at elev + water" per vertex makes boundary triangles slope from the lake level down onto the dry neighbour's ground, coplanar with the terrain there: z-fighting around every lake. (3) River and road polylines run cell to neighbour, i.e. exactly along mesh edges where the two adjacent triangles slope differently; "slightly above the ground" with depth write on gives ribbons half buried and half floating, in 60 deg zigzags. (4) The brush ring is drawn only by the terrain shader, so it disappears under deep water, exactly when the player raises land from the sea or aims a comet.
issues.fix: §6: "Ocean vertices are sea-level independent: aPos = unit direction, aData = (elev, sea ice, 0, 0). The vertex shader places the vertex at radius `uPlanet.x + uPlanet.y` (plus waves) and computes depth = `uPlanet.y - aData.x`. The renderer eases `uPlanet.y` toward `world.seaLevel` at about 1 unit per second. The ocean index buffer may be all of `geo.tris`: it is drawn after the terrain, so land triangles are depth-rejected, and with no sea (level -9) the sphere is entirely underground. Lakes: emit every triangle that has at least one lake vertex, with all three corners at that lake's surface radius, so the shore is a depth-buffer intersection like the ocean's. Rivers and roads: smooth the cell polyline (two Chaikin passes), sample it every 0.5 units or less, put each ribbon vertex at `groundAt + 0.03`, draw with polygonOffset(-2, -2) and depth write OFF. Only the ocean writes depth in drawWater. The brush ring is drawn by both the terrain and the water shaders."

issues.where: SPEC-RENDER §1 `GL.program`, `GL.target`, `GL.mesh`, `GL.instances`, `GL.caps`; §5 Post (HDR fallback)
issues.problem: Small WebGL2 traps that only the gl.js author can fix for everyone. The default `sampler2D` precision is lowp; on mobile GPUs that honour it, HDR texture reads (scene resolve, bloom chain) are clamped to about +/-2. RGBA16F is renderable and multisample-able only after `EXT_color_buffer_float` or `EXT_color_buffer_half_float` is enabled, and its sample limit is not MAX_SAMPLES. A multisampled colour buffer needs a depth renderbuffer with the same sample count or the FBO is incomplete. A multisample resolve blit needs identical formats and identical rectangles and cannot target the canvas. `uniformBlockBinding` on a program that uses no Frame member (blur passes) gets INVALID_INDEX. `mesh` cannot draw a sub-range or grow, but rivers, roads and bolts change size. The terrain needs more than one vec4 of per-vertex data. The RGBA8 fallback clamps "sun-lit white 2.5" to pure white everywhere. Checking link status inside `GL.program` forces serial shader compilation.
issues.fix: Add to §1: "The prepended header also contains `precision highp sampler2D; precision highp samplerCube;`. `caps.hdr`: enable EXT_color_buffer_float, else EXT_color_buffer_half_float, then verify with a 4x4 RGBA16F framebuffer. `caps.maxSamples` = min(4, largest value of `getInternalformatParameter(RENDERBUFFER, <colour format>, SAMPLES)`). `GL.target` with samples > 0 allocates colour and depth renderbuffers with the same sample count; `depthTex` with samples > 0 throws. `blitTo(dst)`: dst is single-sample with the same size and colour format, never the canvas. The Frame binding is skipped when the block index is INVALID_INDEX. `mesh.draw(mode = TRIANGLES, count = mesh.count, first = 0)`; `mesh.update` and `mesh.setIndex` reallocate when given a larger array and update `mesh.count`; `inst.upload(first = 0, count = inst.count)`. `GL.mesh` also accepts `aI0 ... aI3` as extra per-vertex vec4 attributes for meshes that are never instanced. Link status is checked on the first `prog.use()`, not inside `GL.program`." Add to §5: "When `!caps.hdr` the renderer sets `uSunDir.w = 0.4` (`shade` scales sun, ambient and emissive by it), and Post divides exposure by 0.4 and skips bloom."

issues.where: SPEC-RENDER §6 Terrain ("face normal from screen-space derivatives")
issues.problem: Derivative normals are the right call here: an indexed mesh of 40,962 vertices cannot give 81,920 triangles a unique provoking vertex each, and `flat` varyings hit ANGLE's slow provoking-vertex path on D3D11 (Windows). But three rules are missing. If the world-position varying is declared `centroid`, the derivatives are garbage along every triangle edge under MSAA. From orbit a triangle is about 10 px and at the limb it is sub-pixel; the 2x2 derivative quad then straddles several triangles and the normal is noise, which shows as sparkling snow, flickering specular and a shimmering terminator. And nothing says the ocean must not use them.
issues.fix: Add to §6: "The world-position varying is plain `smooth` (never `centroid`). No shader in the project uses `flat` varyings. Facet weight = 0.85 x smoothstep(2.0, 8.0, 1.9 / length(fwidth(worldPos))): fully faceted when a cell edge spans 8 px or more, pure smooth vertex normal below 2 px and toward the limb. The ocean, lakes and cloud shell use the analytic sphere normal plus procedural waves, never derivative normals."

result.verdict: Not ready for a parallel build from the rendering lens. The individual module APIs are sound (the Frame block is all mat4/vec4, 576 bytes with no std140 traps; attributes are float-only; depth precision is fine once near/far are pinned; Post needs no depth texture), but the contracts between render modules are missing: who writes and uploads the Frame block, who binds the shadow map and what a depth program is, how modules see the camera, quality level and each other's data, and the `world.rivers` shape. Those three blockers plus the Objects re-instancing and budget numbers will each be built several incompatible ways. The three decisions most likely to make it look cheap are the undetailed 300 px ground triangles and sparse trees at close zoom, the bloom/exposure calibration that makes the whole day side glow pastel, and the atmosphere split across two authors that will leave a seam on the planet's edge (with 6 px shadow texels at close zoom a close fourth). All 18 fixes are paste-in text; with them applied the documents are ready.

issues.where: SPEC-UI §2 Input ("Power armed" and keyboard bullets), §4 HUD (top bar, power palette, "hide HUD" button), §5 Screens.pause / Screens.timelapse
issues.problem: The phone target cannot be operated. The only ways to disarm a power are "Right-click without dragging, or Escape"; the only way to reach Screens.pause (Settings, Save and exit) is Esc; un-hiding the HUD is `H`; the time-lapse says "Esc exits". The top bar has a menu button (`gear`) that opens `Screens.pause()`. While `Game.hudHidden`, one 44 px `eye` button stays in the top-right corner.
