With a brush power armed on touch, application starts 100 ms after touch-down and only if no second pointer is down; a second pointer at any time ends the stroke and the gesture becomes orbit/pinch/twist until all fingers lift. Touch long-press (500 ms, under 10 px of movement, no power armed) shows the hover tip for that cell or settlement. On touch the brush ring appears at touch-down and the cost/target tip is drawn 64 px above the finger."

issues.where: SPEC-SIM §3.8 `Society.witness(world, cell, ang, { kind, awe, good })`, §3.10 power table and its closing paragraph, §1 Settlement shape, §3.7 `Civ.found`
issues.problem: The faith loop is split between the powers and society engineers with no shared scale. `awe` in `witness` is a devotion delta (devotion is 0..1) but carries the name of the currency whose costs are 15 to 220, and no per-power `awe`, `good` or witness radius is written anywhere. A powers author who passes cost-like numbers saturates devotion at 1 on the first lightning bolt; one who passes 0.01 makes miracles irrelevant against the 2 %/yr drift. There is no novelty decay either, and the spec says "the same meteor watched from far away is pure awe", so a meteor dropped in an empty desert raises devotion in every settlement in range at no cost to love. Under the §3.8 income formula, +0.15 devotion on ten templed towns decaying at 2 %/yr returns about 285 Awe for 150 spent, so harmless wrath pays for itself and mercy has no reason to exist. Initial devotion and love of a new settlement are also unspecified, which decides the whole first five minutes of income.
issues.fix: Paste into §3.8: "`awe` is the devotion (0..1 units, NOT Awe currency) gained by a settlement at the centre of the act; `good` is -1..1; falloff is smooth 1 to 0 across `ang`. Each settlement has a persisted `jaded` (0..1, default 0, decays 5 %/yr): gain = awe × falloff × (1 − jaded), then jaded += 2 × awe × falloff (clamped to 1). love += good × falloff × 0.5. An act with good ≤ 0 gives half devotion to settlements it did not harm." Add `jaded` to the Settlement shape. Add three columns to the §3.10 table (witness ang in rad / awe / good): rain 2×brush / 0.02 per s / +0.6 where moist < 0.3, burning or in drought, else +0.1; bloom 2×brush / 0.02 per s / +0.5; raise, lower 2×brush / 0.03 per s / −0.5 inside owned territory, else 0; lightning 0.10 / 0.05 / −0.6 struck, 0 others; quake 0.20 / 0.12 / −0.8 damaged, −0.2 others; plague 0.12 / 0.05 / −0.7; meteor 0.45 / 0.30 / −1 damaged, 0 others; volcano 0.40 / 0.30 / −1 damaged, 0 others; heal 0.10 / 0.15 / +1; inspire 0.10 / 0.10 / +0.6; prophet 0.15 / 0.20 / +0.5; peace: every settlement of both cultures / 0.10 / +0.8. §3.7: "`Civ.found` sets devotion 0.6 and love 0.3 for an awakened tribe, and copies the parent settlement's values for settlers."

issues.where: SPEC-SIM §3.8 "Awe" (income and aweMax formulas), §4 balance target for Awe, FOUNDATION §5.2 `world.god = { awe: 0, aweMax: 100 }`
issues.problem: The income formula is linear in settlements × tier while costs are flat, so Awe goes from starved to meaningless and contradicts the spec's own target ("a great one every few minutes"). Worked numbers at 1× (2 years per real second): one camp, devotion 0.3: 0.66/yr = 1.3 Awe/s starting from 0, so nothing to do for the first ~12 s and a 76 s wait to fill the bar. Three shrined villages: 1.7/yr = 3.4/s, a meteor every 44 s, and aweMax 175 means volcano (220) cannot be cast at all. Year 1,000 with 20 settlements (8 villages, 10 towns, 2 cities, devotion 0.35): Σ ≈ 19, so ≈ 39 Awe/s, the 1,200 cap is hit, and a meteor is affordable every 4 s (every 0.5 s at 8×). Year 3,000 with 70 settlements: ≈ 150 Awe/s. From about minute 6 there is no spending decision left in the game.
issues.fix: Replace the income line with: "S = Σ devotion × (0.2 + 0.5·shrine + 1.2·temple) × (1 + tier/2) over live settlements. Income per year = 0.6 + 0.9 × ln(1 + S)." That gives ≈ 0.65/yr with one camp, 1.4/yr with three shrined villages, 3.3/yr at year 1,000 and 4.5/yr late (1.3, 2.8, 6.6 and 9 Awe per real second at 1×). Replace the §4 Awe bullet with: "At 1×: a small miracle (≤ 40) every 5–15 s in the Stone age and every 3–8 s later; a great one (≥ 150) every 25–60 s from the age it unlocks. An active `kind` or `cruel` policy is below 90 % of aweMax in at least 60 % of years. simrun prints Awe income per year and the share of years spent at the cap." Keep aweMax as is, and add to the HUD spec: "when a power's cost exceeds `god.aweMax` its tooltip reads 'Your Awe cannot hold this much yet: they must raise more shrines and temples.'"

issues.where: SPEC-SIM §3.10 power definition (`unlock: { phase, age, awe }`) and power table; SPEC-UI §2 keyboard bullet ("one letter per power (shown on its button)"), §4 power palette ("tooltip saying what unlocks them")
issues.problem: The unlock schedule, which is the player's main sense of progress for 35 minutes, does not exist: the table has no unlock column, so the powers engineer invents it and the HUD engineer has nothing to write tooltips from. The hotkeys are also unassigned and owned by nobody: Input must handle them and the HUD must print them, and the natural letters collide with camera keys already bound in §2 (R raise vs zoom, H heal vs hide HUD, Q quake vs heading, E vs heading, A awaken vs orbit) and with each other (plague, prophet, peace; lower, lightning). Edicts are equally unclear to the player: whether they cost anything, how many can be active and whether they can be changed is not stated.
issues.fix: Add `key` to the power definition and two columns to the §3.10 table (unlock: age or aweMax / key): comet, seed, awaken (genesis power of the current phase) — / G; raise — from 'water' / U; lower — from 'water' / J; rain — history start / N; lightning — history start / L; heal — history start / C; bloom — Bronze or 150 / B; inspire — Bronze or 200 / I; quake — Bronze or 200 / K; prophet — Iron or 300 / P; plague — Iron or 300 / X; peace — Iron or 300 / O; meteor — Sail or 450 / M; awaken (history, 250) — Sail or 450 / G; volcano — Industry or 600 / V. State: "Input and HUD read `def.key`; no other letters are bound to powers. The HUD builds the lock tooltip from `def.unlock`: 'Wakes in the {age} Age, or when your Awe can hold {awe}.'" During 'people' Game sets overlay 5 (habitability) and restores overlay 0 on 'history'. During genesis and the time-lapse the sun mode is 'follow'." SPEC-SIM §3.12, replace the progress line with: "`progress` → `{ phase, value, canAdvance, hint, stats: { ocean, veg } }`. value 0..1: molten = 1 − heat; water = sat((seaLevel + 6.5) / 3); life = sat(cover.veg / 0.25); people = 0. hint is a key, not prose: 'cooling' | 'water-more' | 'water-ok' | 'life-more' | 'life-ok' | 'people'. stats.ocean = share of cells that are sea." Raise or lower the land while the clay is soft." plus "Ocean {n} %" with a tick at the balanced level; life "Touch the land to seed it. issues.where: SPEC-SIM §3.10 `comet` row ("large steps at first, smaller as it nears 0"), FOUNDATION §5.2 `world.seaLevel = -9`, SPEC-SIM §3.2 (ocean floor about −6.5), §3.5 vegetation rule
issues.problem: The first thing the player does shows no result. Sea level starts at −9 and the deepest ocean floor is about −6.5, so the first 2.5 units of rise are below every cell: the comet lands, nothing fills, and the step sizes are unspecified so this may last several clicks. The player is also never told how much ocean is a good amount: the gate to 'life' is −3.5, where the continental shelves are exposed and climate (sea cells are the only humidity source) gives a mostly dry world on which the balance targets were never set. Separately, "vegetation never appears from nothing" means any landmass not seeded during the life phase stays bare for the entire game, as does every volcanic island, with no explanation.
issues.fix: Replace the comet effect with: "The first comet sets seaLevel to −6.0 (water pools in the deepest basins on impact). Each later comet adds clamp(0.2 × (0.6 − seaLevel), 0.12, 1.0): 4 comets pass the −3.5 gate, about 12 reach 0, hard cap +1.5. Up to 3 comets may be in flight. The renderer eases the water surface to the new level over 0.8 s." HUD guide (water): show "Ocean {n} %" and a word: under 35 % "a dry, hard world", 35–75 % "a temperate world", over 75 % "a world of islands". Add to §3.5: "Drifting seeds: each year pick 8 random land cells; a plantable cell with veg = 0 that has a cell with veg > 0.3 within 12 hops (sea included) gets veg = 0.08."

issues.where: SPEC-UI §4 HUD top bar and Inspector; SPEC-SIM §3.7 Research, §3.8 The Ark, §3.12 Endings, §4 balance targets
issues.problem: The player is never told what they are aiming for or how close they are. The ending is decided by hidden thresholds on the launching culture's mean devotion and love (beloved ≥ 0.35 and ≥ 0.2, feared ≤ −0.2, forgotten < 0.2), but the HUD shows devotion and love only for one selected settlement, shows no progress toward the next age, and shows the Ark only as a rocket model that grows on one cell of a planet. With the Space-age devotion baseline at about 0.1 × piety and 2 %/yr drift, an unprompted game ends 'forgotten' and the player learns the rule only on the ending screen. The balance targets do not check that 'beloved' is reachable at all. The inspector also hides why a town is starving: `K` and `growth` exist but are not shown.

issues.where: SPEC-SIM §2 events, §3.10 `Powers.can` / `Powers.use` / `awe:short`; SPEC-UI §2 Input (brush ring), §4 HUD (Awe orb, toasts); SPEC-RENDER §10 FX list

The guide covers only the four genesis phases, so nothing ever explains Awe, devotion, why to cast anything or what the ending depends on, and Quick start skips even that. issues.where: SPEC-SIM §3.10 `awaken` ("free, later 250"), §3.8 aweMax formula, §3.12 Endings (`silence`), §4 ("no extinction on at least 9 seeds out of 10"), §3.10 `Powers.natural`

With no settlements aweMax is 100 and income is 0.6/yr, so the 250-Awe `awaken` can never be afforded; the player then watches an empty planet for 50 years (25 s) until the `silence` ending fires, possibly at year 60 of a game they spent four minutes sculpting. The spec's own target accepts extinction on 1 seed in 10 with no player action, and a first camp of about 30 is destroyed below 3 people by a single early drought, quake or wildfire.

Any cell below sea level is sea by definition and a settlement whose centre is under the sea is destroyed, so Lower held on a coastal metropolis at +0.3 kills it in well under a second at any sculpt rate fast enough to feel good in genesis: about 2 to 12 Awe against 150 for a meteor, and nothing says the people witness it. Brush cost is per second regardless of radius, so the largest brush is always correct, and the radius range is not defined anywhere, so Input, HUD and Powers will each pick their own limits.

Brush radius range 0.03–0.15 rad, default def.ang = 0.06 (binding for Game.brushAng, Input and HUD)." `raise`/`lower` row: "Sculpt rate at the brush centre: 1.5 units/s during genesis, 0.2 units/s in history. In history, cost × 4 while the brush centre is on a cell with owner ≥ 0, and the owners witness it per the witness table (the ground moving under them)." This makes sinking a +0.4 coastal city about 2 s and 48 Awe plus fear, and lifting a city out of a rising sea a real decision at 24 Awe/s.

issues.where: SPEC-UI §1 Camera ("Altitude ... from 320 (zoom 0: whole planet with margin)", "fov ≈ 35°"), `Camera.view()`, `Camera.orbit(dxPx, dyPx, viewportH)`
issues.problem: The planet does not fit on the required 390×844 portrait phone. At altitude 320 the eye is 420 from the centre, so the limb is at asin(100/420) = 13.8° off axis. Vertical half-fov is 17.5° (fits), but at aspect 0.462 the horizontal half-fov is atan(0.3153 × 0.462) = 8.3°, so only the middle 59 % of the planet's width is on screen at maximum zoom-out. The Camera has no aspect input at all, so it cannot correct this.

Zoom-0 altitude = R / sin(atan(0.78 × tan(fov/2) × min(1, w/h))) − R: about 320 at 16:9 and about 775 at 390×844, so the whole planet is visible with margin in any orientation. Altitude runs exponentially from that value to 6 at zoom 1; `far` adapts."

Row 2 (12 px text): epithet, people, cultures, temperature and sea change when non-zero. World name is shown only in the pause screen. Bottom: four group tabs (Shape, Sky, Wrath, Grace, 44 px high) and one row with that group's powers (at most 5, each 64×56: icon and cost only; the name appears in the armed chip; no hotkeys). issues.where: SPEC-UI §4 Settlement labels, Chronicle feed; SPEC-SIM §1 Settlement, §2 events (`drought`, `settlement:famine`, `settlement:plague`), §3.8; SPEC-RENDER §6 terrain colour, §10 FX
issues.problem: The player cannot find the things they are supposed to respond to, and has no prompt to choose mercy. Plague, famine, war and blessing are visible only in the inspector of an already selected settlement; half the planet is always hidden; chronicle entries fade. A drought has no visual at all (FX lists rain and storms, not drought; terrain colour is driven by biome and vegetation, which change seconds to years later). So the mid-game crisis is a line of text scrolling past while the player hunts through up to 120 settlements, and the systems already hold everything needed for the people to ask for help.
issues.fix: SPEC-UI §4 labels: "each label carries up to two status glyphs with the name: plague, famine, war, blessed, praying, and 'sea rising' when the centre is less than 0.15 above seaLevel." Add "Now strip": "a compact list of active conditions built from world state at 2 Hz: wars (A vs B), settlements with plague or famine (count), active disasters, prayers; clicking one flies to it and cycles through its places." SPEC-RENDER §6: "terrain colour includes a continuous dryness tint from `moist`; `drought` start and end set need.climate and dirty.color so the land yellows within a second." Yearly, a settlement with devotion ≥ 0.15 prays for 'rain' (famine ≥ 1 or inside a drought), 'heal' (plague > 0.2), 'peace' (its culture at war with exhaustion > 0.4) or 'bloom' (mean scorch of its territory > 0.3); at most 6 at once, largest first. Emit `prayer` `{ id, kind, start }`. If the matching power is witnessed by it while it prays, awe is doubled and good = +1, emit `prayer:answered` `{ id, kind }` (chronicle weight 2). Unanswered after 15 years: devotion −0.05 and love −0.05 once." FX: a thin pale-gold column above a praying settlement, visible from orbit.

Love vs fear, good vs bad (`--good` green against `--bad` red-orange) and up to six cultures are told apart by hue alone. Lightning, meteor and nuclear flashes plus camera shake have no setting. With the default orbiting sun the area under the brush is in night half the time, and at close zoom the tilt-shift blurs everything outside a fixed centre band, which is rarely where the brush is.

SPEC-RENDER: "moonlit terrain keeps at least 30 % of its daylight luminance after tone-mapping. `Post.set.focusY` (0..1, default 0.5) sets the tilt-shift focus band; while a power is armed Game sets it to the pointer's y and multiplies tilt by 0.35."

issues.where: SPEC-SIM §3.11 `Chronicle.snapshot`, §3.12 Endings; SPEC-UI §0 Game loop, §5 `Screens.ending`, `Screens.timelapse`, `Screens.setup`
issues.problem: The payoff moments are undersold and one of them loses data. `ark:launched` sets the ending in the same tick, so the modal ending screen covers the rocket launch, the climax of a 35-minute game, or the player is looking at the other hemisphere. Snapshots are taken only every 25 history years, so the time-lapse of "the whole history of your world" omits its most dramatic frames: molten ball, seas filling, green spreading. There is one autosave slot and Begin on a new world replaces it with no warning.
issues.fix: SPEC-UI §0: "On `ending`, before `Screens.ending`: hide the HUD and set 1×. Type 'ark': fly to the launch settlement (zoom 0.6, 2.5 s), hold 6 s while FX plays the plume and the camera eases back to zoom 0.15, play the ending stinger, fade, then open the screen. Type 'silence': ease to zoom 0 over 6 s with ambience only." SPEC-SIM §3.11: "a snapshot is also taken on every `phase` change during genesis and carries `heat`; `Planet.showSnapshot` renders heat > 0 as the molten crust." `Screens.timelapse`: "weight-3 chronicle entries appear as captions when the scrub passes their year." `Screens.setup`: "if `Save.meta()` is not null, Begin first asks 'This replaces {name}, {year}. Begin anyway?'"

issues.where: SPEC-SIM §3.9 unit speeds, §0.5 TICK; SPEC-RENDER §9 Movers ("at `Units.dirOf`"); SPEC-UI §0 `Game.speed`, §4 Chronicle feed banners
issues.problem: Time scale works against the diorama pillar and against following events. At 1× a settler party moves 5 cells per year = 1.25 cells per tick at 8 ticks/s, about 19 world units per second in 2.4-unit hops. At closest zoom the view is about 13 units wide, so units cross the screen in under a second in visible 8 Hz jumps, and there is no speed slower than 1× in which to watch the miniature world. At 4× and 8× (8 to 16 years per second) a war can be declared and three cities lost while the weight-3 banner is still fading in.
issues.fix: SPEC-RENDER §9: "Movers are drawn at a position damped toward `Units.dirOf` (`DM.U.damp`, lambda 10 per second), never snapped." SPEC-UI §0: "`Game.speed` is 0.25 | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8; 0.25× ('linger', key `0`, 2 ticks/s) is offered in the time controls. With setting `autoSlow`, when a weight-3 chronicle entry arrives at speed ≥ 4 Game drops to 1× for 6 s and then restores the previous speed unless the player changed it; the banner is clickable (fly to cell) for those 6 s."

result.verdict: Not ready for a parallel build from the player-experience lens. Two gaps will break the game as designed: touch has no way to disarm a power, open the menu or un-hide the HUD, and the witness/devotion scale that drives the whole Awe loop is undefined between two owners. Beyond those, the Awe income formula overshoots its own target by 10 to 40 times from the mid-game, the unlock schedule and hotkeys do not exist, the phone camera and HUD do not fit by arithmetic, and the player is never shown a goal. Nearly every fix is a paste-in rule, table or small API, so one revision pass before the build starts should be enough; the specs are otherwise coherent and the genesis flow, chronicle and ending structure are strong.

issues.where: SPEC-RENDER §0/§1/§3/§11 (gl.js, renderer.js, dev/view.html, dev/fixtures.js); SPEC-UI §0 (game.js, index.html, css/base.css, DM.debug); FOUNDATION §5/§6 (state.js, tools/server.js, docs/TOOLS.md, tools/load.js)
issues.problem: There is no build order, but the dependency graph is not flat. Planet, Sky, Objects, FX and Post cannot compile a shader without GL.program, the Frame block and the <lighting>/<clouds> chunks (gl.js). They cannot be seen without renderer.js, dev/view and fixtures, and the viewer needs a DM.Camera.view() that lives in the UI spec. HUD, Screens and Input cannot run without DM.Game, index.html and base.css ("written by the lead", not on disk). Every sim test needs DM.State.create, yet js/sim/state.js, tools/server.js and docs/TOOLS.md do not exist in the tree today (only util, vec, events, geo, load, t, test, shot). All of these are scheduled in the same wave as their dependants, so roughly 14 of 20 engineers start blocked and will improvise private harnesses and GL helpers. Second-order: dev/view.html must "load every existing source file, skipping missing ones", but from file:// a missing <script> is logged as a failed resource load, which tools/shot.js counts as a page error (exit 1). Everyone will run with --allow-errors and mask real shader/GL errors. Also tools/load.js omits js/render/models.js and js/ui/camera.js although both "must also load in Node", so two engineers must edit one shared file.

Stage 0 (lead, before the wave): state.js with tests; tools/server.js; docs/TOOLS.md (shot.js CLI and page API); index.html; css/base.css; game.js as a stub exposing every Game/debug signature; a placeholder for EVERY file named in the three specs containing only the header comment and the empty IIFE wrapper (no page or loader ever references a missing file; `DM.X === undefined` means "not built yet"; each engineer overwrites only their own placeholder and adds no other file); tools/load.js FILES extended with 'js/render/models.js', 'js/ui/camera.js', 'dev/fixtures.js'. issues.where: SPEC-SIM §2 (`phase` "emitted by sim"), §3.3 (`vars.seaBase`, `vars.iceRef`), §3.10 (`awaken`: "the first use starts 'history'"), §3.12 (Sim.genesis.next, Phases)
issues.problem: The step into 'history' has two owners and its side effects have none. Powers is told the first `awaken` "starts 'history'"; the event table says `phase` is emitted by sim; Sim.genesis.next only covers water→life and life→people. Nobody is told to set `vars.seaBase` ("the level when history began"), `vars.iceRef`, or to reset `vars.lifeBoost`. Likely outcome: Powers writes `world.phase = 'history'` directly, Sim never sees a transition, no `phase` event reaches HUD/audio/chronicle, and on the first yearly tick Climate.yearly computes `undefined + ...` = NaN. Then `seaLevel` is NaN, `elev[c] < NaN` is false for every cell, and the oceans vanish. Fixture and test worlds that begin in 'history' hit the same NaN.
issues.fix: Add to SPEC-SIM §3.12: `Sim.setPhase(world, phase) → bool` — "the ONLY code that assigns world.phase. Returns false if unchanged. Performs the entry actions, then emits `phase` { phase, prev }. → 'water': heat = 0. → 'life': vars.lifeBoost = TUNE.sim.lifeBoost. → 'people': vars.lifeBoost = 1. → 'history': vars.lifeBoost = 1; vars.seaBase = world.seaLevel; vars.iceRef = max(1e-6, Σ ice[c] over land cells); world.year = 0. → 'ended': none." §3.10 `awaken`: "after the first successful Civ.found in phase 'people', call DM.Sim.setPhase(world, 'history'); powers.js never writes world.phase". §3.12: Sim.checkEnding and Sim.genesis.next/skip also go through setPhase. §3.3: "If vars.seaBase or vars.iceRef is not a finite number, Climate.yearly initialises it from the current world with the same formulas before use." Acceptance (climate test): a world created with phase 'history' and empty vars survives 400 Climate.yearly calls with a finite seaLevel.

issues.where: SPEC-SIM §3.10 `Powers.update(world, realDt)`, §3.12 tick order, simrun/policies, §4 (`cruel` target); SPEC-UI §0 `debug.ff`, `debug.use`; FOUNDATION §0 Determinism
issues.problem: Comet and meteor impacts happen only inside Powers.update, which is driven by the Game loop with wall-clock dt and is not in the tick order. Every headless driver (tools/simrun.js, policies, debug.ff, DV.tick, Node tests) calls Sim.tick, so a meteor launched by the `cruel` policy or by `debug.use('meteor', cell)` followed by `debug.ff(10)` never lands. The balance target "a cruel player can drive a world to silence" cannot be verified. Brush cost is "per real second" and `power:used` is limited to "4 per real second", yet sim files may not read clocks and policies are given no dt. The contract "same seed + same inputs at the same ticks ⇒ identical world" is also false in the live game, because impact time relative to ticks depends on frame rate.
issues.fix: Add to SPEC-SIM §3.12: `Sim.REAL_PER_TICK = 0.125` (real seconds per tick at 1×) and `Sim.advance(world, ticks = 1)` — "for each tick: Powers.update(world, Sim.REAL_PER_TICK); Sim.tick(world). The only way headless code advances time: simrun, policies, debug.ff, DV.tick and tests call Sim.advance, never Sim.tick. Policies apply brush powers with dt = Sim.REAL_PER_TICK. Only Game's loop calls Powers.update with wall-clock dt." §3.10: "All rate limits and per-second costs are computed from the accumulated dt arguments, never from a clock." SPEC-UI debug.use: "synchronous: brush powers loop Powers.use and Powers.update with dt = 1/60 for `seconds`; click powers then call Powers.update(world, 3) so the comet or meteor has landed before it returns." FOUNDATION §0: "Determinism is guaranteed for headless runs driven by Sim.advance; in the live game impact timing is frame-dependent by design." Acceptance (powers test): use meteor on a settlement, Sim.advance(16), expect `meteor:impact` and `settlement:destroyed`.

issues.where: tools/test.js + tools/load.js (FOUNDATION §6/§7); SPEC-SIM §0.1 ("test stubs do not matter"), §0.2 (DM.world), §3.11 `Chronicle.attach()`; SPEC-RENDER §10 `FX.attach()`
issues.problem: tools/test.js `require`s every test file into one Node process and load.js loads the sources once, so all files share one `globalThis.DM`. The spec invites stubbing (`DM.Society.witness = ...`), but stubs, Bus handlers, TUNE edits and DM.world leak into later files. `node tools/test.js powers` passes alone and the full run fails at integration with no single author at fault. Two further traps. (1) `attach()` is "idempotent"; the obvious boolean-flag implementation subscribes nothing after a test calls DM.Bus.clear(), so chronicle tests silently see no entries. (2) Chronicle handlers "use DM.world" and Sim.create "becomes DM.world", so a determinism test (create A, create B, tick A, tick B, compare) writes A's chronicle into B and fails.
issues.fix: (a) Lead changes tools/test.js to run each test file in its own process (`child_process.spawnSync(process.execPath, [file])`; t.js prints a one-line JSON summary on exit) and aggregates. (b) Add to t.js `T.stub(obj, name, value)`, auto-restored at the end of the current T.test; FOUNDATION §7: "never assign onto DM.* in a test except through T.stub". (c) FOUNDATION §3 and both attach() specs: "attach() keeps the unsubscribe functions returned by Bus.on, calls them, then subscribes again; it must leave exactly one subscription per handler and must work after DM.Bus.clear(). Do not guard with a boolean flag." (d) SPEC-SIM §0.2: "Sim.tick, Sim.advance, Powers.use and Powers.update assign DM.world = world on entry (no rederive), so Bus handlers always see the emitting world." Required test in tests/sim.test.js: two worlds with the same seed advanced alternately produce identical JSON.stringify(State.serialize(w)).

issues.where: SPEC-RENDER §1, §5-§11 and SPEC-UI §1-§7 (no acceptance criteria anywhere); FOUNDATION §7 (Node tests only)
issues.problem: Sim modules have numeric targets; render and UI modules have only "yours to make beautiful" and "must look good". FOUNDATION defines no convention for browser tests: where scenario scripts live, how they run, what they assert, how shots are named. Each of roughly 14 engineers will "prove" their module with an ad hoc screenshot that nobody can re-run at integration. Mechanical regressions (GL errors, NaN matrices at the poles, pick/project mismatch, HUD overflow at 390×844, silent audio) are all checkable by machine with the existing rig (page.errors, decodePng().stats(), Renderer.stats, Audio.renderTest).
issues.fix:
FOUNDATION §7 add: "Browser scenarios live in tests/browser/<module>.scn.js exporting `async (page, browser, args) => result`. Run with `node tools/shot.js --run tests/browser/<module>.scn.js`. They throw on failure, never use --allow-errors, and save shots as shots/<module>-<view>.png." Minimum checks per module (add to each section):
- gl: a program including every chunk compiles; mesh/instances/target round trip; a failing shader's error contains numbered source.
- models (Node): every required name exists; triangle limits; unit normals; indices in range; min y ≥ 0; height = max y; colours in 0..1.
- post: a value-5 quad on black blooms outside its edge; fade = 1 gives mean < 2; non-HDR fallback renders.
- planet: fixture shots at zoom 0 / 0.5 / 0.9, day and night; day-side zoom-0 stats lit ≥ 0.25 and colors ≥ 500; groundAt(geo.dir(c)) = DM.R + elev[c] ± 1e-3; for 200 visible cells Renderer.project then Renderer.pick returns the cell or a neighbour; each overlay changes the mean colour; a sculpt shows up in groundAt on the next frame.
- sky / objects / fx: shot with only that module plus planet; Renderer.stats.instances within budget; emitting every §2 event with a valid payload gives zero errors and ≤ 6,000 particles.
- renderer: draws ≤ 60 and tris ≤ 1.2 M on the fixture at q2; q0/q1/q2 all render; capture returns > 10 kB.
- camera (Node): altitude 320 / 6 at zoom 0 / 1 (± 1 %); no NaN in 10,000 random orbit/zoom/turn steps across both poles; the direction under the cursor is preserved by a drag (± 2 px) at zoom 0.2 / 0.6 / 0.9; eye never below groundAt + margin.
- hud / screens / input: at 1280×720, 1920×1080 and 390×844, no element outside the viewport and touch targets ≥ 40 px; each control produces the expected Game call.
- save: write → reload → read gives an equal serialize JSON; corrupt data → null.
- audio: all 10 renderTest scenarios have nan = false, clipped = false, rms > 0.005, sub/total < 0.25.
Every final report lists commands run, pass counts, shot names, measured numbers and deviations.

issues.where: SPEC-RENDER §11: dev/view.html, `window.DV = { world, ready, cam, tick, frameMs }`, dev/fixtures.js; Renderer.sun; Post grain; FX
issues.problem: The viewer contract is too thin for automated proof. (1) `DV.ready` has no type. The rig's --wait-for polls for a truthy value: a boolean works, a Promise resolving to undefined or a function never satisfies it. (2) Nothing freezes time. The sun orbits on wall-clock time (dayLength 150 s), clouds drift with uTime.z, and stars twinkle, grain and particles animate. Two runs of one scenario give different PNGs and "is the city lit" depends on when the shot fires, so pixel assertions and before/after comparisons are impossible. (3) Fixtures are render-centric: no chronicle entries, snapshots, relations, prophet/edict, status effects or ending, which HUD, Screens.ending, Screens.timelapse and Planet.showSnapshot need. (4) The fixture is the critical path for six engineers yet is owned by the renderer core author, who also owns renderer.js and the viewer.
issues.fix: SPEC-RENDER §11 add: "`DV.ready` is a boolean, false until the world is built and two frames have rendered with every dirty flag consumed. Extra API: `DV.settle(frames = 3) → Promise`, `DV.find(what)` (same keys as debug.find), `DV.pick(x, y)`, `DV.stats()` (= Renderer.stats), `DV.freeze(t)`. DV.tick(n) calls Sim.advance. URL parameters: `t=<seconds>` freezes time (uTime.x and uTime.z pinned, grain off, FX stepped at a fixed 1/60, RAF loop stopped after settle), `sunAngle=<deg>`, `only=planet,sky` (skip other modules), `size=WxH`. With `t` set, two runs must give PNGs whose mean absolute difference is < 1/255. DM.debug gains the same freeze(t)." §0 add: "Static content (stars, tree jitter, settlement layouts, model geometry) uses DM.U.hashf or DM.U.rng(constant), never Math.random; FX uses an Rng that is reseeded on freeze." Fixtures add: ≥ 40 chronicle entries across weights 1-3, ≥ 12 snapshots, a living prophet with an active edict, one war and one trade relation, settlements with plague / famine / blessed / inspire, god.awe 180 of aweMax 400, and `DM.Fixtures.ending(world, 'ark-beloved'|'ark-feared'|'ark-forgotten'|'ark-parting'|'silence'|'silence-ash')`. Assign dev/fixtures.js to its own Stage 1 engineer.

issues.where: FOUNDATION §5.2 `world.dirty` ("the renderer clears each flag after rebuilding"); SPEC-RENDER §4 step 1, §6 Planet.sync ("clear what you handled"), §9 Objects.sync; SPEC-SIM §3.2 Terrain.touched
issues.problem: Dirty flags are single-consumer booleans with two consumers. Planet.sync runs first and clears dirty.elev. Objects places trees and buildings on Planet.groundAt but rebuilds only on dirty.objects, which Terrain.touched does not set. After the sculpt brush, a crater rim, a volcano cone or a quake, trees and towns float above or sink into the new terrain until some unrelated veg threshold flips dirty.objects. Charred or snowy trees need dirty.color, which Planet has also already cleared. Each module is correct alone; the bug exists only when both are loaded. Throttling ("colour rebuilds ~6 Hz", "trees ≤ 2 Hz") makes "clear what you handled" ambiguous as well.
issues.fix: FOUNDATION §5.2: replace the sentence with "Renderer.frame copies world.dirty into `DM.Renderer.dirty` (same keys) and sets every world.dirty flag to false, once per frame, before any sync() call. Render modules read the copy and never write world.dirty. A module that throttles keeps its own pending flags." SPEC-RENDER §6/§9 signatures become `Planet.sync(world, dt, dirty)` and `Objects.sync(world, dt, dirty)`. §9: "On dirty.elev, re-seat existing instances (recompute the radius from Planet.groundAt; no re-layout), at most 10 Hz. On dirty.objects, rebuild. On dirty.color, refresh burn/snow." Planet scenario acceptance: sculpt +3 under a forested fixture cell, settle; every tree instance within the brush has |length(aI0.xyz) − Planet.groundAt(dir)| < 0.05.

issues.where: SPEC-SIM §1, §2 ("society / civ"), §3.3-§3.12; FOUNDATION §5.1 (`rad`, `wet`, `fert`), §5.2 (`world.vars`, transient caches)
issues.problem: Shared state has no single-writer table, so some things have two owners and some have none. `rad` is raised by Society nukes and decayed by nobody (Life.step lists veg, fauna, fert, wet, scorch), so nuked land is dead forever. `culture:died`, `culture:age` and `world:age` are emitted by "society / civ": twice or never. Nobody is told to set `culture.dead`, or to refresh `culture.pop` / `towns`. `world.vars` is a free-form bag written by six modules with no key registry; the 'ash' ending needs "a nuclear exchange in the last 200 years" but no module is told to record it. Chronicle may keep witnessed deeds in `culture._seen`, which is transient and not rebuildable, so epithets reset on every load. `world._fires` is transient with no rebuild hook, so after loading a save with a burning forest the fire[] cells never advance or go out. Sim.rederive has no stated order although Hydro lakes need moist and Life.classify/habitability need fresh.
issues.fix:
Add SPEC-SIM §1.1 "Writers" (binding):
- elev: Terrain.* only.
- slope, coast: Terrain.derive.
- temp, moist, ice, co2, dust, globalTemp: Climate.
- seaLevel: Powers (comet), Climate.yearly, Sim.genesis.skip.
- water, flow, down, fresh, rivers: Hydro.update.
- veg, fauna, fire, scorch, biome, hab: Life (Civ may lower veg when it creates farmland).
- wet: Powers raises, Life.step decays.
- fert: Terrain.generate, Life.step/bloom, Powers.
- lava: Powers.tick.
- rad: Society raises, Life.step decays 1.5 %/yr.
- owner, farm, urban: Civ.
- road: Society.
- culture.age, culture.science, world.age, `culture:age`, `world:age`: Civ.yearly.
- culture.pop, towns, dead, `culture:died`: Society.yearly.
- god.awe: Society adds, Powers.use spends.
- stats.wars: Society.declareWar. stats.miracles: Powers.use. Other stats: Sim.refreshStats.
vars registry: seaBase, iceRef, lifeBoost (Sim.setPhase); rel, lastNuke (Society; Sim.checkEnding reads lastNuke); snapEvery, lastSnap, seen (Chronicle; `seen[cultureId][powerId]` replaces `culture._seen`). Any other key is prefixed with its module name (`civ_...`).
Transient caches: "each module rebuilds its own underscore caches lazily when they are missing (Life.burn scans fire[] > 0; Civ.claim rebuilds _cells; Climate rebuilds _up)".
Sim.rederive order: Terrain.derive → Climate.update → Hydro.update → Life.classify → Life.habitability → Civ.claim for each live settlement.

issues.where: SPEC-SIM §3.7 civ.js, §3.8 society.js, §3.10 powers.js; SPEC-UI §4 hud.js, §7 audio.js + music.js; SPEC-RENDER §9 objects.js
issues.problem: Module sizes differ by about 4×, so a parallel wave finishes when the largest module does. names, path, hydro and icons are one sitting each. powers.js is 16 powers plus comet flight, eruptions with lava flow, tsunami fronts, storms, droughts and six natural-event generators. society.js is belief, Awe, relations, war with armies and battles, trade, schisms, prophets and edicts, nuclear exchange and the Ark. civ.js is the lifecycle API five other modules call, plus food, growth, plague, tiers, 12 buildings, expansion and research. hud.js is nine widgets plus a phone layout. objects.js is the instancing program plus trees plus settlement layouts for 5 tiers × 7 ages × 12 buildings plus movers. Audio is two files under one namespace with no interface between them.
issues.fix:
Split each into two files with the binding namespace unchanged; the lead adds the files to the load order in Stage 0.
- powers.js (LIST, byId, unlocked, cost, can, use, instant effects) + js/sim/disasters.js (extends DM.Powers with tick, update, natural and new `Powers.start(world, type, cell, { power, ang, natural, data }) → disaster`; `use` and `natural` create comet/meteor/volcano/tsunami/storm/drought only through start).
- society.js (newCulture, yearly, witness, raiseProphet, setEdict, aweIncome, belief, schism, Ark) + js/sim/diplomacy.js (extends DM.Society with rel, atWar, declareWar, makePeace, onArrive and new `Society.diplomacy(world)`, called once from Society.yearly: relations, wars, armies, battles, trade, nukes).
- civ.js (found, claim, destroy, damage, capture, at, near, live, canSettle, siteScore, bestSite, TIERS) + js/sim/economy.js (extends DM.Civ with yearly).
- hud.js (top bar, palette, genesis guide, toasts, overlay switch, hover tip) + js/ui/panels.js → `DM.Panels.init()`, `DM.Panels.update(dt)` (inspector, chronicle feed and full chronicle, labels) with css/panels.css.
- objects.js + js/render/towns.js → `DM.Towns.layout(world, settlement, out) → count`: pure, no GL, Node-testable; fills out with `{ model, dir: [x,y,z], scale, yaw, tint: [r,g,b,a], emissive }`.
- audio: music.js exposes `DM.Music = { init(ctx, outNode), update(dt, ctx), stinger(name) }`; audio.js owns the context, the limiter and `DM.Audio.buses = { music, sfx, ambience, ui }`.

issues.where: SPEC-SIM §0.3 (TUNE), §3.7 (age windows), §4 Balance targets, §3.12 simrun
issues.problem: Every §4 target (ages in their windows, 8-40 settlements at year 1,000, Ark between 3,300 and 4,500, 9 of 10 seeds surviving, Awe pacing) is a property of civ + society + life + climate + powers together. No engineer can verify any of them alone, the numbers live in six TUNE blocks owned by six people, and nobody is named to balance after integration. The simrun author cannot run it until every module exists. Civ is told to tune science thresholds to hit age windows without a reference population curve, so the thresholds will be tuned against a private guess and be wrong by an order of magnitude once real growth exists.

SPEC-SIM §4 add: "Balance owner = the sim.js author, in Stage 3. Add `js/sim/balance.js`, loaded last in the sim order, as the only file the balance owner edits: `Object.assign(DM.TUNE.civ, { ... })`. Module authors do not retune after Stage 2." Add reference anchors for isolated tuning: world population ≈ 30 at year 0, 2,000 at 500, 20,000 at 1,000, 200,000 at 2,000, 2 M at 3,000, 5 M at 3,500; settlements 1, 6, 20, 45, 70, 90. Module-level proxies:
- civ: "on the fixture world a lone Stone-age camp of 30 at Civ.bestSite reaches 60 within 60-200 years and plateaus below 400; fed the reference population curve, research crosses each age inside its §3.7 window".
- society: "one camp with a shrine at devotion 0.55 yields 0.6 + 0.55 × 0.7 × 1 ≈ 0.99 Awe/yr".
- life: "with TUNE.sim.lifeBoost, one seeded cell at the centre of the largest fixture continent brings that continent's mean veg/capacity to ≥ 0.25 within 240 ticks on the Life.step(t % 8, 8) schedule".
simrun adds `--hash` (FNV-1a of JSON.stringify(State.serialize(world)); two runs must match) and `--seeds 1-10 --summary` printing a pass/fail table against §4.

issues.where: SPEC-SIM §1 Relation (`Society.rel` "created on demand"), `world.god.deeds`, `settlement.b`; SPEC-UI §4 Inspector ("relations with other cultures"); FOUNDATION §0 Determinism
issues.problem: The inspector will call Society.rel(world, a, b) for every culture pair, and that call creates relation objects inside world.vars.rel. Opening a panel therefore changes the save file and the insertion order of vars.rel. If Society.yearly iterates that object and draws rng per relation, a UI session and a headless run of the same seed diverge, and a bug seen in the game will not reproduce in simrun. The same hazard exists for `for...in` over god.deeds and settlement.b (fixture-built and Civ-built settlements may have different key order) and for unstable sort ties in Civ.near and "largest cities".
issues.fix: Add SPEC-SIM §0.9 "Determinism rules": "(1) Never drive sim decisions from object key order. Iterate cultures and settlements by ascending id, buildings via DM.BUILDINGS, deeds via Powers.LIST. (2) Every sort comparator tie-breaks on id. (3) UI and render code call only read-only sim functions. Add `Society.peek(world, a, b) → relation | null` (never creates) for the inspector; Society.rel is sim-only. (4) Chronicle wording draws from `world.rng.fork('chron:' + entry.id)`. (5) No rng draw may depend on wall-clock time or on whether a renderer, HUD or audio module is attached." Acceptance in tests/sim.test.js: advance 300 years calling Society.peek for all pairs and Chronicle.tale every 10 years; the hash equals that of a run without those calls.

issues.where: SPEC-RENDER §2 Frame block, §3 chunks ("registered by gl.js, used by everyone"), §4, §7 Sky.update, §6 Planet.setOverlay
issues.problem: Only some Frame fields have a named writer (uBrush via Renderer.setBrush, uStorms and uFx.y/z via Sky.update). uPlanet.z/w (cloud and atmosphere radii), uWorld.z (night-light level), uWorld.w (overlay), uFx.x and the moment of GL.frame.upload() have none. Fields will be written twice or left at 0: with Sky absent cloudiness is 0, and with nobody setting uPlanet.z the cloud shell sits at radius 0. The look of clouds and of all lighting lives in gl.js chunks, so the Sky and Planet engineers will need to edit another engineer's file to tune their own visuals. A depth-pass program that includes <lighting> samples the shadow map while rendering into it.
issues.fix: SPEC-RENDER §2 add: "Renderer.frame writes every Frame field each frame except uFx.y, uFx.z and uStorms, which Sky.update writes (Renderer writes defaults 0.5, the sea-cell fraction and zeros when DM.Sky is undefined). Constants: `Renderer.CLOUD_R = DM.R + 12`, `Renderer.ATMO_R = DM.R + 18`. uWorld.z = sat((world.age − 1) / 4). uWorld.w = `DM.Planet.overlay` (set by Planet.setOverlay). uFx.x = 1 − smoothstep(0.55, 0.8, zoom01). Renderer calls GL.frame.upload() after step 1, with the light matrix for the shadow pass, and again with the camera matrix for the scene pass." §3 add: "Chunk bodies belong to the gl.js author and are frozen after Stage 1. Other engineers do not edit gl.js; they request changes in their report or wrap the functions locally. drawDepth programs must not include <lighting>, and Renderer unbinds texture unit 7 during the shadow pass."

issues.where: SPEC-SIM §3.10 power definition and table; SPEC-UI §2 ("one letter per power (shown on its button)", `[` `]` brush size), §4 Power palette
issues.problem: The power definition names fields (name, ang, target, unlock { phase, age, awe }, desc) but the table gives only id, group, kind, cost and effect. The HUD engineer needs names, costs, targets and unlock text before powers.js exists, and the Input and HUD engineers each need the hotkey: three people will invent three tables. The definition has no `key` field at all, and nine letters are already taken (W A S D Q E R F H). The brush size limits for `[` `]` are unspecified.
issues.fix: Add `key` to the power definition and paste the full table into SPEC-SIM §3.10 as data (mirrored by Fixtures.stubs so stub and real module are identical). Keys: comet C, seed G, awaken K, raise U, lower J, rain N, bloom B, lightning L, quake X, plague Y, meteor M, volcano V, heal T, inspire I, prophet P, peace O. target: comet / raise / lower / rain / lightning / quake / meteor = 'any'; seed / awaken / bloom / volcano = 'land'; plague / heal / inspire / prophet / peace = 'settlement'. Default ang in radians: comet 0.03, seed 0.12, raise / lower 0.06, rain 0.10, bloom 0.08, quake 0.08, meteor 0.05, volcano 0.04, others 0. Fill in unlock { phase, age, awe } and a one-line desc for each. SPEC-UI §0: "Game.brushAng is clamped to 0.02-0.20; `[` and `]` multiply it by 0.8 and 1.25." Input and HUD read `Powers.byId[id].key`; neither hard-codes letters.

issues.where: FOUNDATION §6 (tools/server.js on 127.0.0.1:5174, `POST /__save` → shots/), §4 and SPEC-SIM §0.8 / SPEC-RENDER §0 performance targets; tools/shot.js default output
issues.problem: Twenty engineers share one machine. The second `node tools/server.js` fails with EADDRINUSE on the fixed port, or an engineer kills "their" server while others use it. shots/ is one flat directory (names are sanitised to [A-Za-z0-9._-], so no subfolders) and two people will overwrite each other's `test.png`. Timing budgets (tick ≤ 2.5 ms mean, cellAt < 2 µs, 60 fps at 1080p) measured while 20 Node processes and up to a dozen headless Edge instances compete for CPU and GPU will fail at random if asserted in tests.
issues.fix: FOUNDATION §6: "tools/server.js: if the port is in use and `GET /__ping` answers `demiurge`, print 'reusing' and exit 0. Nobody stops a server they did not start. Prefer file:// paths with tools/shot.js; the server is needed only for /__save. Every file written to shots/ starts with the module name (`planet-zoom0.png`)." §7: "Tests never assert wall-clock budgets tighter than 5× the stated target. Exact timings are reported from `T_VERBOSE=1` output or simrun, not asserted. Render performance is accepted on Renderer.stats (draws ≤ 60, tris ≤ 1.2 M, instances) at 1280×720, q = 1 in the rig; fps is measured once, by the lead, at Stage 3."

issues.where: FOUNDATION §5.1 (persisted fields) and §5.3 ("Target size at L = 6 with an empty entity list: under 900 kB of JSON")
issues.problem: The size target contradicts the specified encoding. Persisted bytes per cell: elev 2, water 2, wet 1, veg 1, fert 1, ice 1, fire 1, scorch 1, lava 2, fauna 1, rad 1, owner 2, farm 1, urban 1, road 1 = 19. 19 × 40,962 = 778,278 bytes, which is 1,037,704 characters as base64. That is over 900 kB before any scalar or entity is written. The state.js author will either fail an acceptance check that cannot pass or invent an undocumented compression scheme that Save and the tests do not expect.
issues.fix: FOUNDATION §5.3: "Each persisted field is quantized, then zero-run-length encoded (byte pairs: a 0x00 byte followed by a run length 1-255; other bytes literal), then base64-encoded. The serialized object records `enc: 'rle1'`. Target at L = 6 with an empty entity list on a freshly generated world: under 700 kB." If no compression is wanted, change the target to "under 1.1 MB". Add a round-trip test on a world with random non-zero data in every field.

result.verdict: Not ready for a single flat parallel wave. The sim leaf modules (names, terrain, climate, hydro, life, path) are buildable and provable alone today, but the render and UI layers and the civ, society, units, powers, chronicle cluster have no harness, fixture, stub kit or acceptance criteria. Three contract defects (the rivers shape, ownership of the step into 'history' with seaBase/iceRef, and nothing staged ahead of its dependants) would each break integration. About an hour of lead work on Stage 0/1 (state.js with entity factories and the event table, placeholder files, a Node-loadable fixture with stubs, the viewer and UI harness skeletons, a per-process test runner) plus the pasted fixes to the first six issues would make the documents ready for a parallel build.
